Identify your current moonshot goal right now. Every 6-12 months, scrap everything you built around the prior moonshot, retain the wisdom from that journey, and apply it to the next, larger moonshot.

Eat high-protein with quality fats and quality carbohydrates sourced from fruits and meat. Greg Short personally avoids large quantities of vegetables and finds this dietary pattern keeps him sharp, though he frames this as personal preference rather than a universal prescription.

Spend meaningful time outdoors under natural sunlight each day. Greg Short reports that natural vitamin D exposure makes him feel significantly better and tries to arrange a portion of his day outside.
Actively seek larger markets, larger businesses, larger goals, and larger moonshots whenever a plateau is sensed — do not wait for the plateau to fully arrive.
Be willing to go against the advice of your close circle or family when pursuing a larger challenge or higher-order goal.
Start your e-commerce business on Shopify first to gain a proof-of-concept before expanding to Amazon and TikTok Shop.
Run your initial product batch through consumers and make product tweaks before launching on Amazon to avoid locking in 1-star reviews on an unrefined product.
When you have reached a level where no real peer-level competitors exist, manufacture competition by focusing on critics or perceived rivals to maintain competitive sharpness.

Start by taking on one small battle. Once that is won, aim for one per month, then one per week, and eventually one per day. Do not wait for self-belief to arrive before starting — use the wins themselves as the source of belief.

When your business is not growing after sustained effort, audit whether the obstacle is truly external or whether it is an internal narrative — specifically, identify and question the no's you are telling yourself before concluding the opportunity is closed.
When a genuine external party is saying no, do not accept it as final; continue pursuing — including financially — until they say yes, rather than internalizing their resistance as your own limit.

Before building a new product or brand, audit which distribution channels your target segment's existing competitors occupy; if mass-market retail is unoccupied, treat that gap as the primary opportunity rather than product innovation.
When targeting retail distribution, establish Amazon sales data first to give retail buyers objective demand proof that reduces their adoption risk.
Define your customer avatar not just by demographics but by where they currently cannot find what they need; the gap between where they shop and what they find is the product-market-fit signal.

Stay continuously in touch with culture and community rather than cycling in and out of active market participation; treat sustained engagement as a non-negotiable operating condition for serial product success.
After a major sales event, do not take your foot off the gas: place the next inventory purchase order with the full proceeds before lifestyle temptation can redirect capital.
Execute high-stakes calls, pitches, and meetings every day regardless of how you feel; do not defer based on low energy or bad mood.
Show up and take action 365 days per year to increase your share of good-outcome days relative to competitors who skip when feeling low.
On zero-motivation days, show up physically regardless of how you feel. Do not wait for motivation to arrive before taking action.

When building a bootstrapped consumer brand, identify and invest in a proprietary cultural asset that cannot be quantified or directly replicated by competitors with more capital, rather than trying to match well-funded competitors on ad spend, call volume, or creative output.

In the early years of a business, prioritize building the business over attending networking events or proactively pursuing high-value relationships; once visible scale is achieved, the right people will seek you out.

Schedule regular solo time — individual gym sessions, sauna, or other uninterrupted personal time — and actively limit constant socializing in order to preserve independent thinking, regardless of business stage or social obligations.

When pursuing a dream-spec vehicle or high-ticket durable good, buy a slightly older model at auction rather than new, then redirect the depreciation savings into bespoke customization to produce an exact-fit result.
Commission purpose-built modifications (performance, aesthetics, utility) rather than settling for an off-the-shelf configuration that only approximates your intended use case.
Build branding, marketing, design, and formulation capabilities in-house rather than outsourcing to agencies, starting from day one of the business.
Evaluate any proposed outsourcing decision by asking whether the vendor has enough stake in the outcome to care as much as the founding team does; if not, build the capability internally.

At age 17, audit every major belief and life direction you currently hold and ask: did I arrive at this independently, or did someone tell me to have it? Begin distinguishing inherited programming from genuine self-direction as the first step toward developing free agency.
If you are asking questions about how to think for yourself at a young age, treat that as evidence you are ready to begin — the question itself signals sufficient self-awareness to handle the answer.

When selecting a market, do not confine yourself to the market you already inhabit; map all your passions and find the larger adjacent market where your passion-angle creates white space — where established, data-driven competitors have no emotional investment.
Remove the noise and maintain 100% focus on a single domain rather than spreading mindshare across a diverse portfolio of activities.

Attend industry trade shows and events with the expectation of unknown long-term value; make strong impressions and follow up persistently, because the outcomes of such events are unpredictable and may take years to materialize as major business opportunities.

When entering rooms where you feel culturally or professionally out of place, resist the instinct to acquire the surface markers of that room's norms (dress, jargon, titles); instead lead with the authentic narrative of what you are building.

Before a high-stakes meeting in an unfamiliar institutional context, consult someone already inside that world — not to imitate them, but to understand whether your instinct to conform is necessary or counterproductive.
After absorbing a significant business loss, immediately redirect attention to the next available opportunity rather than processing the loss emotionally.
Show up consistently regardless of motivation; winners are defined by presence under low motivation, not high motivation.
Start entrepreneurship by taking on one small battle rather than waiting until you have experience or a track record.
Sell something that costs you nothing to make other than your knowledge and hard work — an instant-download PDF is the simplest viable form of this in 2026.
Use DM-based selling (social media DM to payment link) as the minimum viable sales infrastructure when you have no website or storefront.
Consider becoming an entrepreneur or intrapreneur in 2026, as the barrier to entry for starting a business is currently at a historic low.
Make time to stay inspired, see what is going on in the market, get outside, and meet people even when your brand is not yet ready for the market.
Define a specific named avatar (e.g., Jim) with behavioral details before making any brand-building decisions; use that avatar as the decision filter for every choice.
Launch a consumer product in whatever packaging can be sourced immediately rather than delay launch to achieve ideal packaging, provided the product inside meets quality standards.
topic: Execution and Rapid Adjustment Over Planning

text: When building a DTC brand in 2026, partner with content creators and influencers rather than commercial content studios or brand agencies.

Give content creators full creative license to talk about your brand authentically, focusing on how they use it regularly to address their own problems — do not script or direct them into a brand-controlled narrative.
Do not measure influencer marketing success primarily by views, impressions, or reach; measure by the quality and authenticity of the creator's relationship with the product.

When evaluating private air travel for business use, prioritize the time saved by eliminating airport overhead (check-in, security, boarding queues) rather than focusing on in-flight comfort or aircraft size.
When entering any international market, work with local people in that country to co-create a product that makes sense for the local culture rather than importing the home-market product unchanged.
topic: Geographic Expansion Sequence: Dominate Local, Then Expand

text: Create discomfort on a regular basis rather than defaulting to the comfort that modern society provides.
Take care of yourself physically and mentally as a foundation for pursuing ambitious goals.
Always go after the challenging next step rather than remaining at your current comfort level.
Level up your growth goals continuously rather than settling for targets you can already achieve.
Identify any category of your life where you are behaving like a coward — where fear is causing inaction — and immediately go after that thing.

Narrow down to one business model and take one concrete output action today (e.g., set up your first Google Business listing, launch your first Shopify ad, make your first cold call, publish your first video) rather than planning further.
Treat every unit of output (video, ad, listing, cold call) as a piece of real estate being stacked; focus on volume and iteration rather than optimizing each piece before publishing.
Every time you feel the urge to switch business models or research a different opportunity, recall the cost of the model-switching loop and return to current output tasks instead.
Double down on whatever output format or product generates positive feedback signals; do not pre-optimize before feedback exists.

Use SEMrush's keyword overview tool (SEO tab > Keyword Overview) to check monthly search volume for a service-plus-city search term. Exclude branded searches (searches for specific company names) and look for a minimum of 1,000 organic searches per month before targeting a city.
topic: Market Selection Criteria: Growth + Pain + Targeting

text: Register the Google Business Profile name as the primary domain (e.g., 247plumberchicago.com) and verify the domain is unregistered before listing it on the profile; listing a taken domain will link to a competitor's website.

Use CallRail (~$50/month) to buy a forwarding phone number for each city's profile so that the number can be re-forwarded to a call-answer hire without changing the public-facing number on the listing.

After a contractor takes payment on-site from a customer, call the customer immediately to verify the amount charged — framing the check-in as an account system issue (e.g., 'Our QuickBooks had an issue, just confirming you were charged $X'). This prevents undisclosed upcharging without confronting the contractor directly.

Compile review text that includes the service-plus-city keyword naturally (e.g., 'I hired these guys to send a plumber out to my house in Chicago — they fixed my drain within two hours'). This embeds geo-relevant keyword signals into the review text, which reinforces Google Maps ranking for that location.

Maintain a shared Google Calendar or daily morning text with the primary sub-contractor so that at the time of call booking, the operator already knows whether that contractor is available for the requested time slot — preventing over-booking or delayed dispatch.

When filling in Google Business Profile sections (description, products, services), use ChatGPT to generate keyword-rich content incorporating the service-plus-city phrase throughout every available text field.

Have every prospect fill out an intake questionnaire before your sales pitch that surfaces their current weight, dream goal, prior attempts, and pain points — this forces them to confront their pain multiple times and pre-frames you as someone who cares.
Never sit across a table from a prospect during a sales conversation; position yourself shoulder to shoulder to eliminate adversarial distance and increase rapport.
Greet every prospect emphatically by name within 10 seconds of entering the building; this signals high service quality before any sales conversation begins.
Require gym members to review your gym on Yelp, Facebook, and Google as a condition of completing your front-end program (but not to leave a 5-star rating — that violates trade practice rules).

Hold member social events every 21 days (not announced as recurring) and require all new members to attend; offer to cover babysitting and let members bring a friend for free to generate warm referrals.
Conduct daily 10-minute team huddles covering previous day sales, cancellations, attendance red flags, and client wins to keep staff focused on business growth metrics.

Do weekly 30-minute one-on-ones with every team member, asking primarily what is going well, what is not, and how you can help them win more — listening rather than telling, so the team member arrives at conclusions independently and owns the outcome.
When switching gym clients from unlimited to 3x/week sessions, offer time slots in reverse order of popularity (least crowded first) to naturally spread attendance without mandating it.
Introduce every new gym member to a veteran OG member in their first week and pair them as workout partners, to accelerate the social connection that drives retention.

Create two simultaneous programming tiers for every workout session — Tier 1 (advanced) and Tier 2 (regressive with same movement patterns) — so new and experienced members can train together without awkward beginner-only sessions.
Hire for every key gym role before you need it so you have time to find the right person and train them; never hire out of desperation, which compromises quality and leverage.
To change bad habits, modify your context before attempting to change behavior through willpower.

Analyze your calendar and org chart to identify which activities you spend time on and which lack leverage. For any large cluster of low-leverage activities not owned by anyone on the org chart, create a new role and hire someone.

Do not claim or celebrate hard work as your competitive advantage. Instead, claim excellence in recruitment, culture building, team leverage, and leadership. These create compounding returns across the organization.

Recruit people with complementary skills, not clones of yourself. Identify the core functions your business needs (marketing, sales, product, operations) and hire specialists for each, not generalists who try to do everything.
As CEO, every hour spent must be replaced with an activity that builds the business even more. Continuously identify the next bottleneck and solve it, rather than optimizing existing operations.
Build a farm system of talent underneath the executive team so that you can always promote from within and never be dependent on external recruiting. This creates sustained competitive advantage.

When a customer comes to you upset, immediately get into character: validate the severity of their complaint, take ownership as if you personally failed them, and position a quick solution. Never downplay or minimize.
For high-ticket purchases, create a continuity service (annual checkup, maintenance, storage, conditioning) to convert price-shopping one-time buyers into dealer-for-life repeat customers.
When positioning a recurring service, use an insurance analogy to a familiar product (e.g., car insurance) to frame the cost as protection rather than luxury.
Structure upsell closes by embedding the base offer into your question so that the customer's automatic no-response confirms yes on what you want to sell.
Create small products or bonuses from your waste materials (sawdust) to use as free entry incentives that drive customers in the door and make them receptive to paid upsells.
Signal artificial scarcity via dealer-only access, customer limits, final-sale language, and fixed-capacity queuing to create perception of demand and justify premium pricing.
Build your business by executing the same fundamentals every day: email follow-up, content creation, sales team building, blog maintenance. Scale comes from compound discipline, not from shortcuts.

Brands entering TikTok should not attempt to replicate their existing campaign formats; they should release their authentic brand voice in the platform's native idiom, accepting imperfection and avoiding over-engineering.

Brands with a product that solves a functional problem should position their TikTok content around the problem-solving use case rather than brand messaging, participating in the platform's how-to ecosystem rather than interrupting it.

Advertisers evaluating TikTok should measure product-discovery outcomes (trial rate, brand switching) rather than standard awareness metrics, because the platform's primary commercial mechanism is discovery-led behavior change rather than awareness-led recall.

When AR sits at $500k-$600k and is constraining growth, approach a bank for a 90-day rotating AR revolving credit line; present collection rates and financial diligence to qualify for rates around 1% per month.

Before changing a business model to solve a perceived financial problem, diagnose whether the root cause is a cash timing issue (solvable with financing) versus a structural unit economics problem (requires model change).

When evaluating a revolving credit line for AR financing, confirm you have a repayment discipline: pay down the line immediately when AR is collected, not after a delay, to avoid the credit line compounding into a debt trap.

When building a buy-and-hold portfolio, prioritize acquiring businesses at higher revenue scale (e.g., $20M+ ARR) rather than smaller businesses ($3M or below) to reduce the probability of retaining a founder whose ambition is already exhausted.

For a portfolio operator with available capital but time constraints, identify the single highest-leverage activity that enables all other objectives (e.g., brand-building / demand generation) and hire dedicated operators to manage portfolio companies day-to-day.

Generate deal flow for acquisitions through outbound prospecting, trade shows, and conferences rather than waiting for inbound leads; treat deal flow generation as a separate operational process from portfolio company management.

Before removing a founder post-acquisition, ensure a high-caliber replacement is in place, because founder-dependent businesses embed tacit knowledge that cannot be recovered once the founder departs.

Diagnose whether a growth-stalled business is constrained by demand (not enough leads) or retention (losing customers too fast) before committing to ad spend increases — the intervention differs entirely.

Map the expectation-setting chain across marketing, sales call, and onboarding offer to identify where the promise-delivery gap introduces churn; close each gap in sequence starting with the earliest stage.

When fixing churn in a recurring-service business, hire a customer success professional from the SaaS or software world who has experience building systematic success pathways rather than relying on sales or marketing talent.

For a local service business considering multi-location expansion, benchmark annual churn before scaling ad spend — if churn exceeds 20% annually, fix retention first to protect local market reputation and addressable pool.
Install attribution tracking on all paid ad channels before increasing budget; require the third-party ad manager to provide channel-level attribution or replace them with one who can.
Scale ad spend in incremental steps (e.g., double before tripling) rather than jumping to the target level, so each step can be evaluated against attributed results.
Do not open a new customer segment (e.g., commercial) or build a new acquisition system while existing channels are unoptimized and un-attributed.

Script every interaction a sales rep will have with a customer — from how they walk into a property to what they say at each stage of the sales conversation; no ad-libbing should be permitted until the script is proven.

Fill available desk capacity with new hires as quickly as possible rather than waiting for the perfect regulatory or facility situation to resolve; 4 empty desks represent ~50% immediate growth capacity.

Do not delay scaling investment in recruiting and training until after a facility expansion is complete; begin shifting time toward hiring and developing agents while the office transition is still in progress.

Hard-block 25% of founder time for team development and training, even if it means accepting a ~$1M annual personal billing reduction, as the leverage from improving multiple reps exceeds the personal production loss.
Before taking a business to market, mentally switch sides of the table: imagine you just bought your own business today and identify every flaw you would immediately fix. Then fix those things first.

When building early influencer relationships, pay in the currency the influencer values most (fame, reach, co-branding) rather than defaulting to cash; lead with a genuine value exchange before making any promotional ask.

Always find and enlist the person who has already built the business you are trying to build; buy their decades of accumulated knowledge through a hire or relationship rather than re-living their learning curve yourself.

When founding a capital-light startup, define the single 'kill shot' constraint that would end the business if unsolved (e.g., how to ship perishable meat) and resolve that constraint before committing resources to anything else.

For subscription businesses, evaluate per-unit profitability with all variable costs fully loaded (materials, packaging, shipping, payment processing, consumables) rather than using a stripped-down gross profit figure.

When entering a new local market for B2B professional services with no existing network, start paid ads ($100-200/day) immediately alongside the organic outreach playbook rather than waiting for organic traction first.

For commercial real estate lease negotiation, only accept projects above a minimum deal size so that the dollar-savings proof number is large enough to anchor prospect perception in marketing materials.
In commercial real estate advisory ads, anchor on total dollar savings over the full lease term rather than percentage savings to maximize perceived value magnitude.
Use LinkedIn as the primary digital outreach platform when targeting C-suite executives in a new market, as it reaches decision-makers in a professional context aligned with their buying mode.

When a referral-partner channel is producing 60-70% of new revenue, do not pivot to a new channel type — invest in expanding the number of partners in the existing channel before testing new acquisition methods.

Before adding a secondary service line to support deal conversion, test whether the core deal can close without it by piloting a cohort of deals that use introductions to third-party providers rather than in-house delivery.

When positioning tax-advantaged real estate to high-income earners, anchor the value proposition on the guaranteed tax benefit (e.g., 58% effective return on tax dollars redirected) before discussing property management or Airbnb income, so the management layer is perceived as supplementary rather than load-bearing.
Audit your sales script before attributing a talent shortage to thin market supply — a consultative or judgment-heavy script artificially inflates the skill requirement for every role in the org.

When recruiting for sales director roles focused on training and culture (not closing), source candidates from door-to-door sales management backgrounds where team-building and high-volume rep management are already proven.
Target a span of control of approximately 10 reps per sales director; split into two directors at 7-8 reps each rather than letting one director manage 15.
Use a proven sales training handbook (e.g., Gym Launch sales handbook) as the director onboarding curriculum rather than building a custom program from scratch.

Before investing in technical attribution infrastructure, survey your existing customers directly and ask: where did you first hear about us? Tally results by channel and use the plurality answer to identify the primary discovery channel for reinvestment.
topic: Audience Survey for Discovery Channel Attribution

text: When studying top sales or advisory performers for duplication purposes, observe their specific behaviors and language rather than asking them to explain why they succeed; their explanations will not reflect what actually drives their performance.

Apply the scientific attribution rule: give last-touch credit when conversion happens within 30 days of a touchpoint; give first-touch credit when the gap exceeds 30 days. Use this blend to avoid over-optimizing toward direct response at the expense of brand channels.

Once the primary discovery channel is identified via survey, allocate more than double your current investment to that channel while holding all other brand touchpoints at their current levels rather than cutting them.

When clients request unscheduled founder time, route them to a documented resource or to the next available calendar slot rather than responding immediately; this retrains client behavior away from ad-hoc requests.

When announcing a delivery model change to existing clients, lead with new information that has come to light, state the decision the new information requires, explain the actions that follow, and list multiple specific benefits to the client.
Before changing the selling model of a supply-constrained business, first resolve the delivery constraint (hire, delegate, restructure sessions) to ensure supply can meet the new demand level.

If your coaching or education business has both a high-value skill-delivery component and a lower-value consumable ongoing component, price them separately: charge a high price for the skill or transformation, and a near-zero or nominal price for the recurring consumable access to the network or content library.

To find a brand manager for a creator or coaching business, identify brands you admire, use LinkedIn to find the specific media or brand operators behind those brands, and directly reach out offering to pay more than they currently earn.

For a financial advisor coaching company, reactivate new clients by targeting their existing list and facilitating their first sale within the first seven days of onboarding to achieve time-to-value and anchor them to the product.

Before launching national expansion or paid advertising, calculate whether your existing local market is actually saturated by testing whether you could serve 3-5x your current volume within existing infrastructure.

Do not respond to a competitor undercutting you by reducing prices to existing customers; instead, focus on delivering superior outcomes to your existing base and let the competitor discover their own unit economics.
Keep passive investments (real estate, REITs, funds) with professional partners who run them independently; do not let passive investments become active management obligations.

When scaling a service business with a supply constraint, raise prices 20-40% backed by a performance guarantee before hiring additional staff; use the resulting cash flow to fund redundant headcount.
Separate inbound and outbound sales into structurally distinct teams; make inbound lead access a career milestone earned by top-performing outbound closers.
When entering a new inbound lead channel, route all leads to a single proven closer rather than distributing across multiple reps to minimize confounding variables during iteration.
Do a 15-minute time-study for one full week, logging every activity; rank each by revenue contribution and uniqueness, then delegate the bottom half to existing or hired team members.
Run national recruitment ads with a relocation package (e.g., $25K at hire + $25K at month 6) to attract specialist talent when the local talent pool is insufficient.
In the $1M-$3M revenue swamp, increase volume on the single working acquisition channel before opening new channels; use the resulting cash surplus to fund channel diversification later.

When two businesses have materially different margins and growth trajectories, consider exiting the inferior one quickly at a discount rather than winding it down slowly, because founder attention freed immediately compounds faster in the superior business.

Classify employees as W-2 rather than 1099 if they show up on a schedule, attend required meetings, and perform work according to your specifications; do not attempt to reduce compliance cost by misclassifying employees as contractors.
Track weekly outbound recruiting outreach volume as a primary metric before evaluating any other recruiting lever.
When facing a talent bottleneck, increase recruiter headcount first (target 3x current) and track outreach volume per recruiter per week.
Negotiate bulk placement deals with recruiting firms (5+ placements per firm, discounted rate, extended replacement guarantee) to access multiple candidate networks simultaneously.
Frame a talent acquisition budget as a capital allocation decision by calculating gross profit per hire and enterprise value created, not just the cost line.

When facing a fork between expanding geographically versus deepening home-market share, ask: what state can generate the same revenue as your home market? If the answer is none, default to home-market domination first.
topic: Geographic Monopoly: Fix State Before Expanding

text: Before initiating any business change, explicitly calculate whether the potential upside is at least 50% above baseline to justify the guaranteed ~20% performance cost of change.
Identify the monopolistic levers available in your current market (key relationships, proprietary tech, brand density) and exhaust them before evaluating expansion to adjacent markets.

Remove the word 'coach' from your vocabulary if your intent is to build a scalable franchise model; position yourself as an online educator whose audience is the top-of-funnel for franchise sales, not consulting clients.

To validate that a brick-and-mortar service model is nailed independently of founder social media, test whether it can acquire customers and sustain margins using only paid advertising at normal industry CAC rates (10-30% of revenue for brick-and-mortar).

Build a gamified technician career advancement system that creates a visible path to six-figure income; this retains technicians, reduces turnover costs, and drives the customer retention and premium pricing that sustains high net margins without personal founder involvement.

Position AI-produced commercials as equivalent to traditional broadcast production quality, withhold the AI method, and price at broadcast market rates ($400K-$500K) to capture the full arbitrage margin.
Add media buying as a single-headcount service line to complete the full-service offering for mid-market advertisers — creative production plus distribution under one retainer.
Qualify mid-market ad agency clients by requiring at minimum one year of profitable advertising history, $1M+/year in ad spend, and existing target CPAs before onboarding.

Stop leading with the AI angle in sales conversations; instead pitch the output (more creative, faster, cheaper than building an internal team) and let the AI production remain an invisible efficiency lever.
Talk to the AI (referencing a Scribe or GPT-style tool) before an in-person consulting meeting so the AI has context on your business situation and can contribute relevant ideas during the session.

When you are the most expensive option in your market, accept that you will lose price-sensitive clients and do not lower prices in response; invest in a better sales process to attract and close the non-price-sensitive segment instead.

For a service business at $1-3M revenue with multiple customer segments, audit which segment has the highest LTV-to-CAC ratio and re-orient all marketing, messaging, and offer design toward that segment.

In sales to corporate or enterprise clients who attempt to commoditize your service, proactively reframe the conversation from per-project price to total organizational cost (including buyer time, switching costs, and coordination overhead).

Replace a 70-page bespoke product catalog with three clearly named bundle tiers (e.g., small/medium/large or chicken/fish/steak) and train the sales team to route clients to the nearest fit rather than building custom proposals.

When building an education business, add consumables (monthly resources, tools, or community inputs) to create recurring revenue and LTV, because knowledge transfer alone has no retention hook once the curriculum is complete.

Before choosing between the corporate-brand path and the information/coaching path, map out 10 years of annual income under each scenario; do not let the romanticism of a terminal exit obscure the compounding value of higher annual income.
If pursuing an exit, build the corporate-brand path; if prioritizing annual income, build the coaching or licensing path; do not attempt both simultaneously.
For promotion-heavy service businesses, hire your first employee specifically to take over delivery work so the founder can dedicate 100% of available time to sales and marketing.
topic: Founder Time Redeployment: Delivery to Marketing

text: When designing cold outbound attraction offers for B2B services, use a decoy structure: offer something free that feels complete but frames a larger paid system as the real solution, making the upgrade feel like the obvious choice.
When seeking a first operations hire at the ~$5M revenue stage, offer a relocation package or signing bonus to attract candidates from outside the local area if the local talent pool is insufficient.
When designing profit-share structures, set explicit three-tier performance lines: below target (termination risk), on target (OTE), and above target (upside cap) before presenting the offer.

For phantom equity grants, include a minimum tenure requirement (12-24 months present at time of sale) and a clawback clause (interest reverts to zero on voluntary departure) before presenting the structure to a prospective hire.
Never email a quote to a residential contracting customer; always present the price in person and collect the deposit at the same visit.
On the initial phone discovery call, give a wide anchor range (e.g., $5,000-$50,000) rather than a specific number, and explain that a precise figure requires an in-person site visit.
After calculating your normal cost-plus price for a job, add 20% to that number before presenting it to the customer.
Incentivize the sales rep with an extra 2% commission on jobs closed and deposited at the in-person visit to reinforce the new close-on-site behavior.
Remove the phrase industry average from your vocabulary as a benchmark; use your own prior-period performance as the only relevant comparison.

When evaluating whether to take on a large B2C volume opportunity alongside an existing B2B business, model the revenue at 1%, 2%, and 5% close rates before deciding — the math makes the decision obvious.
If your referral close rate is dramatically higher than your cold close rate on the same offer, install a sales motion before investing in any other marketing or lead generation activity.
Treat an insurance-mandate distribution deal as a lead generation channel, not a sales shortcut — model it as lead gen with required closing, and build the sales infrastructure accordingly.

When managing a list of founder-only tasks that are infrequent and low-leverage, audit the list, categorize each by frequency and replaceability, and systematically outsource to contractors or VAs on a piecemeal basis, trading founder hours for management overhead until a single coordinator can manage all contractors.

For e-commerce businesses seeking to expand paid traffic beyond current audience, use a keyword research tool to identify problem-aware and unaware search terms adjacent to current product-aware keywords, build an advertorial bridge page, and test those keywords at a budget sufficient to generate statistically meaningful click data before scaling.

When building a brand in e-commerce, lead with brand investment rather than legal protection of the product, because brand scale is the precondition for successful legal enforcement; a small operator pursuing patent litigation against well-funded dupes will be outspent before the case resolves.

When training live-commerce or sales presenters, write every coaching instruction in observable physical terms (raise voice, increase pace, square shoulders) before using any trait descriptor (charisma, energy, confidence); only assign trait labels after specifying the behaviors that produce them.

For service businesses, treat all after-tax profit that is not needed for personal living expenses as an experimentation and reinvestment budget, not as income; allocate it primarily to talent acquisition and brand-building activities rather than personal consumption.

When evaluating whether to self-operate a warehouse or outsource logistics, first test whether the logistics operation is a stated competitive differentiator for your customers; if it is not, treat it as a commodity cost center and transfer it to a 3PL so founder attention can concentrate on the primary value-creation activity.
Before sending a contractor to their first job, verify that their schedule can absorb the job volume you intend to give them (1-3 jobs per day) and confirm they agree to the revenue split.
Confirm that the contractor speaks the same language as your customers fluently enough to communicate without friction on the job site.
Ask to see a contractor's Google Business Profile for negative reviews before committing to working with them.
After a contractor completes a job, ensure they send you the invoice and any payment receipts before you consider them verified for ongoing use.
Do not send a review request link to a customer until you have confirmed by phone that they are satisfied with the service.
Use a VA to handle post-job customer satisfaction calls and review requests to reduce manual overhead at scale.
Have every contractor sign a ChatGPT-generated agreement explicitly stating they are fully liable for any damages caused during the job.
Place referral-only terms and conditions on your website stating the business connects contractors with homeowners and bears no liability for outcomes.

To attract higher-spending, more advanced customers, create lead magnets and advertising content that addresses the specific problems those advanced customers actually experience. Do not use beginner-facing hooks and then try to upgrade those leads.
When shifting to a higher-value avatar, simultaneously adjust pricing upward to match that avatar's willingness to pay.
When changing your target avatar, plan for a re-baseline and relearn period; do not judge the new strategy against the old avatar's metrics.
Ensure full congruence across all funnel layers: the ad hook, the content, and the lead magnet must all speak to the same level of problem and audience sophistication.
Give a GM a small profit share they can earn into rather than awarding it upfront; structure the share to escalate with tenure so retention and performance incentives compound over time.
Install tracking and measurement systems during the GM onboarding overlap period, when the founder still has bandwidth; do not defer data architecture to a later phase.
Before signing a lease or committing capital to a second location, complete a three-to-six month founder-absence test at the first location and use any performance dip as a hard stop signal.
For privately held brick-and-mortar locations, target GM all-in compensation of roughly $100k OTE with a range from $75k (underperform) to $120-130k (exceed KPIs).
Create a video sales letter (VSL) for your company that sells it as a product to prospective recruits — treat talent acquisition using the same conversion mechanisms you use for customer acquisition.
Make your free content better than everyone else's paid content to maintain brand credibility; if free quality drops, the entire conversion funnel above it loses its foundation.
When deploying excess business capital into real estate, raise funds from your existing audience base to create dual value: returns for them and co-investment alignment with the brand.
Design future investment bets (ventures, PE) to serve your existing distribution base rather than requiring net-new customer acquisition from scratch.

When running a profitable business, focus all management attention on growing core profitability (e.g., $5M to $6M profit) rather than pursuing side projects or passive income streams, because profit growth at a 10x+ multiple creates greater wealth than income accumulation.

To unlock billionaire-scale thinking, reverse-engineer from the wealth goal ($1B) backward to required assets ($70-100M EBITDA), then to required top-line revenue ($300M at 30% margin), then to transaction size and volume required daily, weekly, and monthly.

When building for billionaire scale, evaluate opportunities only if they (1) do not depend on founder's time to scale, (2) address markets large enough to sustain $100M+ EBITDA, (3) generate 50%+ gross margins, and (4) operate on 5+ year time horizons. Avoid $50-100M capped opportunities.

When selling a CRM or automation tool to Instagram fitness coaches, open the lead magnet video with a seven-minute walkthrough showing exactly how followers are converted to customers without manual DMing; brevity and specificity both reduce friction and raise perceived credibility.

For a GoHighLevel reseller seeking channel partners among fitness business coaches, test at least three distinct hooks (e.g., recurring revenue angle, churn prevention angle, compounding LTV angle) at sufficient spend before declaring which message resonates, then concentrate all spend on the winning hook.

When moving to an intermediary channel model (selling to gurus/agencies rather than end users), build two separate customer success functions: one managing the intermediary relationship and one managing the end-user experience, because the two sets of problems and escalations are structurally distinct.
Test and pursue business ideas that appear illogical or counterintuitive to conventional wisdom, rather than screening for prior logical coherence.
When evaluating markets, check whether customers are actively complaining about a problem; their silence may indicate an unmet latent need rather than market indifference.

Use Twitter as a public brain dump for ideas rather than emailing yourself privately — this converts private brainstorming into testable public content that also provides fast feedback via retweets and replies.

Create 5 or more variants of each call-to-action (book mention, review ask, share request, event promo, lead magnet) and rotate them to prevent audio blindness; keep each CTA to 5-10 seconds to avoid being skipped.

Place call-to-actions at the beginning, middle, and end of content (and additional mid-roll points in longer content) to maximize the chance that any given listener or viewer is exposed to at least one CTA.

To fix a cold sales rep, have a live current client hop on and share their experience rather than retraining technique — the testimonial restores conviction, which is the actual root cause of the performance drop.

Train sales reps using a question-based framework rather than a feature-recitation script; the base script is: 'Why are you here? What have you struggled with in the past? Why didn't that work? I think you might be a good fit — can I tell you about it? Does that make sense? We can move forward.'

For the One-to-Ten close: ask the prospect to rate their readiness 1-10; then ask what would it take to make them a 10; then also ask why they are not a 1 — the second question gets them selling you on the product's value.

Match the personality type of a sales recruit to the type of sales environment: high-volume transactional sales requires hunters; long-cycle enterprise sales requires farmers — mismatching these is a common recruiting failure.

When building the 'how I' content frame, talk about what your clients did and the framework you built for them rather than what the audience should do — this grounds the claim in documented experience and eliminates the credibility attack surface.

Set end-of-day (not end-of-week) as the default turnaround time for all work deliverables unless explicitly stated otherwise — this compresses project cycle times roughly 7x and compounds into ~40x annual output differential over peers with end-of-week defaults.

Document the journey in real time (vlog, podcast, written) rather than retrospectively — the value is greatest when lessons are captured with the specificity that comes from immediacy, and it creates an archive that compounds in credibility as the business grows.

When in a conflict with someone whose behavior seems irrational or malicious, reconstruct their reinforcement history — what did they get rewarded or punished for over their lifetime — before assigning moral blame.

Write down striking ideas immediately when you encounter them, even in social or impaired states, because the reflection period required to extract their full meaning is long and memory is unreliable.

When messaging service providers found on Craigslist or Facebook Marketplace, frame the partnership carefully: explain that you're paying for marketing and lead generation, that you want the provider to benefit from ongoing work and customer retention (not one-time exploitation), and that you're willing to split margin to keep costs low and volume high.

Use software to generate unique phone numbers for each Google Business profile so that inbound calls can be attributed to and tracked by individual profile, revealing which geographic locations and profiles are performing best.

Research the pricing of service providers in your local market on Craigslist, Facebook Marketplace, and Google second-page results; use their rates as the baseline and mark up pricing at least 2x to maintain 50% gross margin.

Bootstrap Google Business profile setup by using photos of your own work or your provider's past work, and solicit initial reviews from friends or family to seed the profile credibility before organic customer reviews arrive.
Prioritize hiring a call manager as your first employee once inbound call volume reaches 50+ calls per week; this hire removes the time bottleneck that prevents scaling to passive income.

Set up and maintain multiple Google Business profiles across different addresses within your city to capture search traffic from all geographic zones; each profile should be treated as a separate passive income asset.

Introduce yourself, explain your credibility, and explain why the viewer should listen to you in every piece of content — even if long-time viewers already know you — because warm viewers appreciate reminders and cold viewers need the introduction.

Avoid inside jokes, unexplained references, and content that assumes prior audience familiarity; fully explain all references so that a viewer encountering your content for the first time can follow along without feeling like an outsider.

Repost your single best piece of content from the prior year; given audience turnover and growth, a significant portion of your current audience has never seen it, and it will likely perform as well or better than new content.

Track paired metrics for any business function: pair a quantity metric (e.g., views) with a quality metric (e.g., RPM or customer satisfaction rating) so that optimizing one cannot come at the complete expense of the other.
Invest in pre-production research (topic selection, structure, language) rather than fixing structural problems in post-production editing; an ounce of pre-work eliminates a pound of post.
When building educational content, use visualizations (charts, data, on-screen text) that clarify the subject matter, rather than visual effects that entertain but do not enhance comprehension.
Narrow your content topics to match precisely the interests of the audience you most want to serve commercially; broad topic coverage attracts audiences who will not convert into your core offer.

Upon waking, before engaging with the day, systematically apply the grandfather frame: imagine your 85-year-old self reviewing your current life through your current body, then consciously notice and appreciate moments that your older self would find irreplaceable (physical sensations, relationships at early stages, small routines, even mundane environments).

When facing business stress or anxiety about outcomes, shift context by asking: from my 85-year-old self's perspective, does this matter? Does it change how I value the work itself? Use this to downweight short-term status or dollars and focus on the intrinsic experience of doing the work.

Reflect on past seasons of life (periods of hardship, heavy work, constraint) and retrospectively reframe them using the grandfather lens: what does your younger self doing difficult work look like from the vantage point of appreciating finitude? Find gratitude in the fact that you did it, not resentment about the difficulty.
topic: All Life Paths Have Equal Suffering; Outcome Differs by Choice

text: Before presenting a product, ask the prospect for explicit permission to explain it; the permission request signals respect and reduces resistance to the explanation that follows.
Present products only in terms of the experiences the buyer will have as a result, using analogies; never lead with features.
Stack sales appointments immediately after visible proof moments (e.g., client result events, testimonial reviews) to temporarily elevate team conviction and close rates.
When a prospect raises an objection, respond with a curiosity question ('tell me more about that') rather than a rebuttal; guide the prospect to resolve the objection themselves.
In sales, define your role as the person who knows how the conversation should go, and lead it there through structured questions rather than chasing the prospect's unguided narrative.
Expose sales teams regularly to testimonials and transformation stories from clients they personally closed to maintain conviction between training drills.
Use cold calling to rapidly obtain entry-level employment: target 100 calls, expect 10% resume requests, close 1%, and aim to begin work within 2-3 days.
Delegate tasks priced below your hourly rate to offshore labor at 1/3 the cost, freeing founder time for higher-value acquisition and scaling work.
Build skill demonstrations in public (social platforms) with no expectation of immediate monetization; use the portfolio effect to attract inbound offers.
Pivot business models within weeks if initial market fit is weak; minimize sunk cost and preserve founder conviction by exiting fast.
Once sustained profitability is achieved across multiple streams, consciously eliminate low-alignment business lines to concentrate founder effort on the highest-conviction opportunity.
Before stating a high price in a sales conversation, say: 'Before I say the price, it's super expensive' — then pause, let the prospect reset their internal anchor, and then deliver the price.

If you close 80% or more of your sales calls, raise your prices by 3-4x before running any other optimization; do not attempt to improve close rate or offer quality until you have tested price at the higher multiple.
To serve wealthy clients optimally, engineer your service to be faster, easier, and guaranteed; pre-do the work that requires effort from the client rather than asking them to do it.

Explicitly communicate in your marketing that you cater exclusively to a high-wealth or high-revenue client type; self-selection will filter out unqualified prospects and increase close rates without changing the offer.
Sell to wealthier clients rather than increasing volume of budget clients; fewer expensive clients produce more revenue, less friction, and more referrals upmarket.

To calculate your CAC, take your total annual marketing and sales-related spending (advertising, sales commissions, marketing labor/contractors) and divide it by the number of new customers acquired in the same year.

To calculate LTV (lifetime gross profit), take total annual revenue divided by total active customers to get average lifetime revenue per customer, then multiply by your gross margin percentage (revenue minus cost of goods or delivery, divided by revenue).

Run the LTV/CAC improvement exercise on your business: (1) Can you raise price? (2) Can you decrease delivery cost? (3) Can you add an upsell? (4) Can you add a downsell for unconverted buyers? (5) Can you add a cross-sell? (6) Can you add financing? (7) Can you change payment collection terms to front-load cash? If you cannot rapidly answer all seven for your business, you do not understand your business model well enough.

To improve CAC, focus on: (1) improving your core offer's compelling nature; (2) producing more and higher-quality ad creatives with better hooks and winner remakes; (3) conversion rate optimization (split-testing landing pages, follow-up sequences, and sales scripts); (4) training the sales team if phone sales are used; (5) advertising on platforms or audiences with lower CPMs — but never optimize for lowest absolute CAC without also tracking LTV, because cheap leads are often low-quality customers.

For any business, identify your 30-day customer value (gross profit collected within 30 days of acquisition) and your CAC, and compare the two numbers before making any decision about marketing channels or tactics. If 30-day gross profit is less than CAC, fix the model before increasing ad spend.
At age 20, live as cheap as possible (roommates, minimal lifestyle) to maximize the gap between income and expenses.
Allocate 100% of excess income (after living expenses) to education that increases earning capacity: courses, coaching, mentorships, workshops, seminars.
Spend $2,000 per month on educational purchases rather than investing in S&P, real estate, or passive vehicles.
Follow potential teachers' free content (Instagram, YouTube) for 7 days before purchasing their paid courses to validate quality.
When purchasing courses, approach each as a single brick in your entrepreneurial degree, not as a standalone savior.
Buy courses from multiple teachers in the same field to synthesize comprehensive knowledge rather than relying on a single source.
Replicate a proven method exactly before iterating on it; copy the bricks first, then earn the right to modify.
Identify which skill brick is missing from your bridge and focus your learning attention there to accelerate progress.
Write four to five hours per day before starting other business activities to protect the creative writing window from displacement by operational demands.
Use Hemingwayapp.com to get immediate grade-level and adverb feedback on prose as you write, to train simpler writing habits through real-time reinforcement.

Eliminate any sentence from a paragraph that can be removed without changing the paragraph's meaning; use shorter sentences over longer ones; use shorter words over longer ones; eliminate adverbs and replace them with more precise verbs.
Use only simple tenses in writing (e.g., 'wanted' instead of 'would have liked to') to reduce cognitive load on the reader.
Send a manuscript to four to eight beta readers whose opinions you value and who will not withhold honest criticism, then act on convergent feedback and ignore divergent feedback.
When writing a story, deploy all five senses (smell, sound, sight, touch, and sensation) to set the scene through description rather than direct statement.
Structure a book around three to six big buckets that address a single narrowly defined problem, then anchor each bucket with a personal story that explains how you learned to believe in that bucket.
When writing a book, add stories at the points where the instructional content starts to feel heavy to the reader, then return to the instructional content after the story provides context.

When a logical inconsistency or a real-world counterexample is discovered in a working draft, go back to the beginning, adjust the underlying assumptions, and restart the draft rather than patching the inconsistency locally.

Do not justify material luxury purchases on the premise that they will create external motivation or increase work discipline. The purchase decision should be pre-made based on existing financial capacity.

Only purchase a depreciating asset like a car in cash if the full purchase price can be recouped within 2-3 months from current income, or 4-5 months maximum, without disrupting business reinvestment.
Distinguish between motivation-to-acquire (chase phase) and post-purchase satisfaction. If using anticipation as motivation, prepare for reduced psychological reward at purchase completion.

Take all discretionary effort, money, time, and resources and direct them toward one skill or domain every single day for an extended period; do not distribute effort across multiple simultaneous pursuits.
When learning content creation, produce high-volume output (hundreds of posts and tweets) and take feedback from each piece without stopping; treat it like athletic drills, not creative expression.
Assess your own tolerance level (high, medium, or low) by observing how long it takes for hardship to change your behavior, then use that self-assessment as the baseline for improvement.

Develop explicit categories for high-ROI spending above $100k/year: prioritize purchases that eliminate chronic annoyances, buy back time, or fund meaningful long-term impact rather than defaulting to luxury consumption that delivers diminishing returns.
Define your customer avatar with as much specificity as possible — age, goal, weekend routine, car, which influencers they follow — before selecting any marketing channel or influencer partner.
Surround yourself with people from younger generations who are on top of emerging digital trends; they activate new platforms before established operators recognize the opportunity.
Regularly look at yourself and make sure you are not becoming who you do not want to be; the entrepreneurial grind has a documented tendency to erode family and personal values without awareness.
When evaluating a mentor or equity partner, look at their life model (marriage, family, personal health) not only their enterprise value or financial track record.
Identify any category of life where you are behaving like a coward (avoiding something out of fear) and go after that thing without waiting for a perfect environment.

Brands advertising on Pinterest should plan seasonal campaigns significantly earlier than on other platforms — Christmas campaigns, for example, should begin in April or May to reach users in the planning mindset before intent has crystallized.

Advertisers should treat Pinterest ads as content additions to the user's experience rather than as interruptive placements; the test is whether the ad could plausibly be pinned by the user to their own board.

Platforms committed to user well-being should build safety and inclusivity features directly into product design (e.g., skin tone filters, mental health routing) rather than relying on post-hoc content moderation alone.

SMEs and niche retailers should upload their full product catalog to Pinterest to benefit from intent-based discovery by users who are in an open planning mindset before brand decisions have been made.

When sourcing contractors for on-site trade services, search Google for businesses on the last pages of results and Facebook Marketplace groups where tradespeople post asking for extra work; these low-visibility contractors are most likely to accept the operator's split terms.

When negotiating contractor rates, frame the operator's role as handling all advertising and marketing (even if the operator uses organic-only methods), and offer the prospect of steady volume (e.g., three jobs per day) as the value proposition in exchange for accepting a lower per-job rate.
For high-ticket drop-servicing jobs, always collect the full operator markup as a deposit before any work begins, so profit is captured at approval rather than at completion.

Invoice customers directly through the operator's account (Stripe, Square) and separately remit contractor payment after customer payment clears; this keeps payment flow under operator control and enables clean record-keeping.
For low-ticket services, use a contractor intake form specifying the payout range upfront so contractors self-select based on willingness to work at that rate, reducing negotiation friction.
When identifying which BSL skill is your growth constraint, invest as much cash as possible into buying access to experts in that specific skill before addressing the other two legs.

When entering a conversation with no clear desired outcome, ask: 'What behavior would I like someone to start, stop, or change as a result of this conversation?' If no answer exists, cancel the meeting.
When starting with zero assets to sell, begin by defining what to sell, then immediately learn to sell it; avoid spending time on logos, websites, or branding until those two things are working.
Use competitors' negative user reviews as a research tool for discovering the pain points your advertising should address and the language your target customers actually use.

When deploying capital into self-investment, identify the single BSL skill most constraining your growth at the current moment and direct maximum spending there — do not spread across all three simultaneously.

Set a bank-account watermark (e.g., $5,000) and invest everything above it automatically — or alternatively, commit to a fixed monthly investment amount (e.g., $2,000/month) and live on the remainder; pick either approach and execute it without exception.
Buy a used car that is approximately 10 years old and pay for it outright; avoid car payments entirely throughout early wealth-building years.
Allocate 1–10% of monthly income as a mandatory learning budget spent on skill experiments, accepting that many experiments will not immediately pay off.

When entering a paid learning community or mastermind, give disproportionately — offer 4–6 hours of your highest-skill work to every other member — to generate the reciprocal knowledge exchanges that justify the entry fee.

Frame every small income gig (DJ event, helping a friend move) as an investment worth 13x its face value in retirement purchasing power, to lower the psychological threshold for taking on additional income-generating activity.

When allocating capital or time in your business, map every initiative to one of three outcomes — more customers, higher LTV per customer, or lower risk / higher reliability — before committing resources. If you cannot articulate clearly how an initiative achieves one of these, treat it as a candidate for elimination.

If your business profit is approaching $5M annually, resist selling immediately; spend one additional year growing to $8M+ and shoring up key risks before going to market, as the size premium and compounding multiple effects can triple enterprise value for one year of patience.

Evaluate whether a $100K investment in systems and technology could re-categorize your business from traditional service to tech-enabled service, and calculate the enterprise value impact (additional multiple turns times annual profit) before comparing that deployment to putting the same capital in a passive market index.
When buying real estate as an investment, focus on geographies with continuing population inflows or higher birth rates to ensure the appreciation leg of the return thesis is structurally supported.

Service providers should operate with the conviction that their product is the best quality and most elite offering in their category. Do not compromise on quality messaging even if pursuing premium pricing.

When serving wealthy clients, make yourself available through multiple contact channels (email, phone, WhatsApp, text) and respond with maximum speed (same-day or faster). Speed and convenience should be the service differentiator, not price reduction.

To appeal to rich customers, accomplish the same service delivery in half the time. Whether dry cleaning, advertising management, or other services, speed is the premium differentiator that justifies high pricing.

Price products and services at the premium tier ($50,000+) rather than competing in the bargain or best-value segments. Premium positioning attracts lower-demand customers and generates margin for reinvestment in quality.
Reinvest margin into hiring senior talent, improving delivery experience, and refining the product. Avoid the trap of competing on price; instead, use higher prices to fund superior execution.

Begin influencer outreach by contacting people you already know personally before attempting cold outreach; even a small mutual follower count or prior interaction materially increases response probability.
When asking your network for influencer introductions, explicitly offer to pay a referral bounty for introductions that convert into partnerships, and state the dollar amount upfront.

Set your social media bio to clearly state that you partner with influencers and describe what type of partnership you are seeking, so any influencer who views your profile understands your intent immediately.

Prepare mock-ups of what the influencer's brand would look like on your product (or of the product you would create for them) before the first meeting; bring physical samples or demos if a tangible product is involved.

Structure influencer partnership economics so the influencer visibly gets the better side of the deal; make your side of the obligations larger and more costly so the influencer feels they are receiving outsized value relative to their effort.

If budget is tight, offer to fly out and meet the influencer in person at your own expense; frame the travel as incidental ("I'm out that way all the time") to avoid making them feel they are inconveniencing you.

Reach out to the same influencer across every platform simultaneously (Instagram, LinkedIn, TikTok, email, direct mail); the platform where they have fewer followers gives the highest inbox-signal-to-noise ratio and the best chance of standing out.

Prepare financial projections for the influencer before the pitch: estimate their current follower count, post frequency, assumed reach-per-post, assumed 1% click-to-buyer conversion, and project a 12-month revenue outcome to show you actually did the math.
Focus on becoming the most authentic version of yourself rather than modeling or copying another person's approach, style, or content.
Before creating content or teaching, first do notable things (achieve outcomes or accumulate high-volume effort), then talk about what you learned — do not start with talking.
When you lack proof, start by working for free: acquire 10 free clients using a free-trial-plus-penalty structure to generate real experience and documented results.
When building a personal brand, ask: who do I provide the most value to, and what unique insights have I gained from my own context or domain?

If you have under $100k in savings: stop eating out (discount groceries only), stop buying new clothes (Goodwill only), attend only free friend events, and use remaining time to apply for higher-paying jobs, pick up side hustle work, or learn skills that pay a higher hourly rate.
When entering a new job or sales environment, find the hardest worker in the room and double their input level — if they make 100 dials, make 200.
Set an alarm to go to sleep on time rather than setting an alarm to wake up; it is hard to wake up late when you go to bed at 9pm.
Before giving up on learning something, set a 20-hour timer and actually attempt the task for 20 hours; most things are not hard — they are simply unstarted.

Humble yourself to people who are more experienced even if you believe you have greater raw processing speed; ask questions, offer value in return, and treat their advice as paid mentorship obtained for free.
Use action as a coping mechanism for impatience with outputs: whenever you feel anxiety about results not arriving fast enough, direct that energy into increasing input volume rather than ruminating.
Review your top 10 content pieces or sales calls from the last month; identify one thing they share that the bottom 10 lack; implement that one characteristic in every future attempt going forward.
Evaluate every person in your life using a single filter: does having this person in my life make it more or less likely that I hit my goals? Remove those who decrease the likelihood.
Before starting a business in a new category, pay to join a mastermind or community of existing practitioners in that category to learn what not to do before committing capital.

When someone fails to complete a task, walk them through the five-reason Management Diamond in sequence: Did you know what I wanted? Did you know how to do it? Did you know the deadline? Were you not motivated? Was something blocking you? Identify which nodes are active and fix each one separately.
topic: The Execution Gap: Knowledge Without Action

text: When giving a performance improvement directive, frame the conversation goal at the outset: explain that the purpose is to increase the likelihood of a specific behavior occurring, not to make the person feel bad. This framing filters out emotionally punishing content that is counterproductive.
Before accepting any abstract claim someone makes in a conversation, apply Logic-Evidence-Utility: What does this term mean behaviorally? What is the evidence? What action does this imply?
topic: Undefined Words Create Mythology and Prevent Clear Thinking

text: Create role-specific behavioral checklists for training. If two employees produce different results on the same role, compare their checklist completion. If checklist completion is identical but performance differs, treat the checklist as incomplete and update it rather than blaming the underperformer.

To identify what motivates a specific employee, learn their history of reinforcing stimuli: what they have been most deprived of (praise, autonomy, money, status) determines what will motivate them now.

For roles with long feedback cycles, artificially insert shorter intermediate feedback loops (milestone check-ins, micro-rewards for sub-tasks) to sustain motivation through the full project timeline.
When training fails, do not repeat the same instruction. Instead, lower the assumed prerequisite floor: identify which sub-skill the person is missing and start instruction at that level.

When you feel an impulse to counter-punish an employee in the moment, ask: what do I want to have happen? If the answer requires future influence over this person, choose the response that increases influence rather than the one that satisfies the immediate emotional impulse.

Alex Hormozi recommends that first-time founders always start with their own money rather than outside capital, to ensure mistakes are paid for with personal funds rather than those of investors, family, or friends.

When evaluating a business for investment at Acquisition.com, Alex Hormozi first identifies the theory-of-constraints bottleneck before committing any growth capital, to avoid inflating the upstream queue at an unresolved downstream constraint.

Alex Hormozi recommends that when investing, focus only on markets and business types where you have genuine insider knowledge of the industry, so that post-acquisition operational guidance and value acceleration are based on earned edge rather than generic management.

For operators who have built a profitable bootstrapped business and are reinvesting profits, Alex Hormozi recommends computing the return on invested capital for each new unit (e.g., new gym location) before deciding whether to reinvest in the core business versus deploy capital elsewhere.

When facing a setback, apply the Cosmic Relevance Frame automatically: situate the problem within astronomical scale (planet, sun, galaxy, expanding universe) to dissolve acute emotional affect before choosing a course of action.

When facing a recurring frustration or inconvenience, apply the Veteran Frame: ask yourself what you would feel about this same inconvenience on the one-thousandth occurrence, then choose to feel that way now.

Build a personal toolkit of cognitive reframes specifically designed to compress recovery time after adversity; identify which tools activate fastest and practice until they become automatic default responses.

When inflating the importance of social judgment, imagine your own funeral in concrete operational detail (food quality debates, venue temperature complaints, people checking off guest lists, dinner afterward) to restore accurate perspective on how briefly others hold any individual in active attention.
When building an education business, explicitly define screening metrics for customer fit and reject applicants who do not meet those criteria, even if they have a credit card.
Publish aggregate outcome data (median, top 20%, average, disaggregated by category) rather than hand-picked success stories or income testimonials.
Give away all core curriculum content for free across multiple platforms; monetize the implementation, coaching, feedback, and accountability layer instead.
Maintain brand standards by ranking graduates by performance and being willing to exclude poor performers from endorsement or completion, even if they paid.
Spend at least one year building thought-leading free content before expecting brand-based pricing power or selective admission to work.

Before building toward an exit, search for M&A activity in your specific business category on Google to confirm buyer demand exists and to identify which attributes those buyers value in comparable transactions.

Think of your business as a product and a potential acquirer as the customer; design features (recurring revenue, faceless operations, documented leadership) that this customer explicitly pays premiums for.

If you teach people to run a type of business, standardize their operations with shared systems, price points, and branding upfront so that the top performers can be rolled up into a group exit later without requiring retroactive standardization.

When building a licensing or affiliate-based business that could resemble a franchise, audit the combination of name, system, and fee: ensure you remove at least one element to avoid legal franchise classification and the associated regulatory requirements.

If you are a creator whose audience greatly exceeds your available capital, consider selling a small minority of your distribution holdco to fund product inventory and launch logistics rather than waiting to accumulate capital organically.

During onboarding, have new sales reps listen to approximately 40 good recorded sales calls before taking any live calls. Track completion via call-review software that logs whether the rep actually watched each recording.
Role-play with trainees every morning during the 14-day onboarding period, focusing on the script. Only graduate them to a half live-call schedule after they pass the role-play test.

Listen to rep call recordings at 2x speed and take written notes before the 1-on-1 coaching session. Bold or prioritize only the top 1-2 highest-impact improvements to communicate on the call; do not overwhelm with every error.

After each 1-on-1 coaching session, send the rep a written summary of the specific items discussed so there is a trackable record. Use a tab or tracker for each rep showing the date and the items assigned each week, then verify improvement on the next weekly review.
Maintain a visual leaderboard that is always up to date and visible to the entire sales team to foster competitive motivation.
Set the PIP expectation and the bottom-10% quarterly cut rule at time of hire so reps understand the performance floor before they start; frame it as the price of being on a world-class team.

Run an optional early morning team training huddle daily. Make attendance mandatory for trainees and reps on a PIP. Observe that high-culture teams will have voluntary near-universal attendance even from tenured reps.

Boil down every offer's sales close to one binary decision (e.g., 'Can we help you make more money in excess of our fee than you'd make on your own, yes or no?') and write it into the script so reps are directing every call toward that decision.

Sales managers should exemplify every standard they require of the team: arrive first to every meeting, complete the daily checklist, follow the pipeline hygiene rules. Lead by example as the visible embodiment of team standards.

Screen for ambivert communication style in sales candidates: look for someone who listens actively, speaks when appropriate, and is socially aware. Candidates who dominate the conversation or motor-mouth are poor fits.

When you want to buy a discretionary item you cannot rationally justify, take the delta between what you can afford with existing resources and what the item costs, then identify a defined, time-bounded way to generate that delta from underutilized existing assets (spare time, underused relationships, dormant skills) before making the purchase.
topic: Fast Cash Plays via Underutilized Assets

text: If you take on debt for a discretionary purchase, confirm in advance: (1) you can pay it off within one year, (2) there is no prepayment penalty, and (3) you have a specific written plan for how you will generate the repayment funds.

For any discretionary purchase you know is consumption rather than investment, explicitly label it as such before funding it, and draw only from new incremental income sources rather than from core income distributions, savings, or new debt.
Stay ahead of spending by keeping lifestyle costs flat while growing new-money income relative to each new defined purchase, rather than expanding lifestyle proportionally to income growth.
Stop eating out entirely; buy only from discount grocery stores to minimize food costs during the capacity-building phase.
Wear only the clothing you already own for the next two years; if absolutely necessary, trade or buy from thrift stores (e.g., Goodwill).
Live as cheaply as possible during the capacity-building phase: ideally with family, or with other cost-minimizing roommates, sharing bedrooms if needed.
Stop doom-scrolling and reclaim the 5am-9am and 5pm-9pm windows outside of employment for skill-building and future-business preparation.
topic: Time Block Architecture for Dual-Track Growth

text: Before building a product, build a waitlist: let people commit their time first as a signal of purchase intent.
