If you want to enter a field, move to its geographic hub (finance to New York, film to Hollywood, politics to DC) rather than attempting entry from a distance.
Spend all excess cash on skill acquisition until you cannot find any more skills to buy; treat yourself as the highest-return asset.
Be conscious of what you are trading and what you are trading it for before making any significant life or business decision.
When evaluating criticism of your goals or methods, first assess the critic's achievement in the relevant domain; if they have none, discount the criticism entirely.
Articulate your worst-case scenario as a specific, concrete outcome rather than a vague fear, then assess whether that outcome is survivable; most are.
Frame past hardships as necessary prerequisites for your current position rather than wasted time, to eliminate regret without requiring that the frame be objectively verifiable.
Set up ACH payment processing with your merchant processor if you don't have it already, because it provides a backup payment path when credit cards are unavailable.
Always request ID before requesting a payment method during closing.
Make a light observation or joke about information on the prospect's ID (e.g., hometown, age) to reinforce rapport while handling their payment method transition.
Use the phrase 'let me trade you for the card you want to use' instead of 'give me your credit card' to frame payment as an exchange rather than a demand.
Physically shake the ID back toward the prospect's wallet or purse to non-verbally indicate they should expose their payment methods rather than asking explicitly.
When a prospect says they don't have the desired card, ask 'Do you have your phone on you?' and walk them through pulling their banking app and statements before defaulting to other alternatives.
If Apple Wallet is not available or the prospect refuses ACH, offer to charge an alternative card and delay the payment 24 hours so they can swap the card at home.
When using the delayed-payment approach, set a mutual phone alarm with the prospect for the time they will be home and available, so you can call them as a reminder to swap the payment method.

When writing an RFP response or opening a B2B sales conversation, set the value frame in the first paragraph before the buyer anchors on price. State explicitly that the goal is the highest ratio of dollars-in to dollars-out, not the lowest input cost.

Attach a case study from the most comparable prior client to every RFP submission. If the client cannot be named, whitewash the attribution with as much identifying meta-detail as confidentiality allows (industry, city, company size class). Use the 13-point proof checklist to ensure all possible proof elements are included.

Include a consulting rider clause in RFP bids offering any additional one-time consulting services at a 25% discount during the contract term to create a foot-in-the-door for ongoing revenue expansion once the initial budget is approved.

Treat every B2B sales conversation as a synthetic RFP by simultaneously addressing both the RFP floor (minimum requirements, price compliance) and the value ceiling (total business impact, ROI on the differentiating factors the buyer actually cares about).

Identify your top two or three differentiated performance dimensions (e.g., speed, risk reduction, retention rate) and get quantified statistics that demonstrate the cost of those outcomes on a global or system-wide level, not just a per-unit price.

When sourcing contractors via Facebook community posts, message the individual contractors who drop their phone numbers (not the formal business postings), as they represent direct worker availability rather than business gatekeeping.
Search for Facebook posts in your local area asking "Does anyone know a reputable [contractor type] in my city?" and message the contractors who respond in the comments with their phone numbers.
Use Indeed job postings rather than Facebook Marketplace when sourcing contractors, as Indeed attracts higher-quality applicants seeking structured work.
Call businesses directly with phone numbers posted on Facebook rather than calling Google My Business listings, which route to gatekeepers.
Join contractor-specific Facebook Groups in your local market and post opportunities directly; contractors actively monitor these groups for work.
When contractors respond with hesitation or hostile questioning, deprioritize them and focus on contractors who express straightforward availability and eagerness to work.
Spend discretionary non-core time (e.g., 5-9am blocks) building a gated community of your exact target avatar rather than on short-term prospecting activities that leave no residual asset.
When running a podcast that features target-avatar guests, invite all past guests to join a private gated community as an exclusive benefit, using the podcast relationship as the seeding mechanism.
Structure the community so that you (the broker or founder) are the explicit gating function for membership admission, to preserve scarcity and maintain elevated perceived status relative to members.

When designing a consulting retainer model over commission income, pair the retainer with a bundled software or tool benefit (e.g., free Yardi access) to increase perceived retainer value and reduce price resistance.
Evaluate every non-revenue time block by asking: in two years, what tangible asset will I have to show for this work? Discard activities that produce no residual asset.
When you roll red, pick up the die and roll again. Do not stop to analyze whether the die is fair or whether others have better dice. The only productive response to a failure is the next attempt.

When comparing yourself to a peer who is ahead, stop at the diagnostic step — what are they doing that I am not doing, and how do I learn it? Do not continue to the labeling step — concluding that you are worthless or permanently inferior.

When you identify that you built something wrong (hired the wrong leader, established the wrong team culture), make the change even if it means going two steps back. Refusing to make it because of the short-term pain guarantees permanent operation below your potential.

Learn how to behave in hard circumstances early; the hardships that come with growth will require the same behavioral standards at higher stakes. The behavior must be trained before the stakes are high enough to make it costly to fail.

When joining a group or community, commit to becoming the top performer in the group; identify the status game being played and use your existing skills to add value to every member, freely and without asking for anything in return.

When learning a new skill inside an employer's business, explicitly communicate to the employer which skills you want to develop; use that clarity to find environments that will invest in your growth, and leave environments where the employer refuses to teach.

If making educational content, only teach skills you have personally implemented and have documented results from; use a documentation (building in public) phase before transitioning into instruction to build credibility before claims of expertise.

To outperform a more experienced competitor in the same role, do at least twice the input volume they do; because they already have skill advantages, matching their effort leaves you permanently behind, while 2x inputs eventually close and surpass the gap over a five-to-ten-year timeline.
topic: Effort Compounds Relative to Starting Conditions

text: When evaluating whether to switch business vehicles, account for the full compounding reset cost of restarting in a new vehicle rather than only comparing the upside scenarios of each; stay in the current vehicle unless the new vehicle's leverage multiple is provably large enough to overcome the reset.

Stay within your existing industry when pivoting rather than switching to an entirely new one; industry experience compounds as an invisible skill floor that makes up the majority of the advantage most people think is model-specific.

Record the business video starting at your local street sign, move to your company vehicle (with business name visibly printed), show tools or business equipment in the vehicle, and start/unlock the car. Keep the entire video concise and focused on each of the three verification requirements.

When creating a Google Business Profile for a service area business, include the target city in the business name (e.g., 'Salt Lake City Plumber' instead of just 'Plumber') to improve local relevance and reduce geographic broadness.

Use a tracking phone number (CallRail, GoHighLevel) for your Google Business Profile contact number if you do not have a dedicated business line, ensuring all inbound calls are captured and trackable.
Always ensure the business name on your vehicle signage, business cards, and Google Business Profile submission match exactly to avoid verification rejection or suspension.
For address-based (not service-area) business profiles, obtain a qualifying physical address in the target market to receive the local ranking boost that address verification provides.
Build and rank profiles in multiple geographic markets using the same verification and ranking system, rather than trying to dominate a single market, to scale revenue linearly.
Source contractors who will execute the work sourced from your ranked profiles, and negotiate a commission structure (e.g., 40% of each job) so you earn without handling service delivery.
Prioritize profile ranking optimization (reviews, post frequency, keyword optimization) over technical SEO expertise, as Google Business Profile ranking operates on its own local search subsystem.
Distribute Google Business Profiles across multiple Gmail accounts rather than consolidating them under one account owner.
Avoid editing multiple profile fields (name, address, phone, website, service category) simultaneously; space out edits across different sessions when possible.
When submitting documentation for reinstatement appeals, print documents first, then photograph them rather than submitting digital files.
Prioritize government-issued documentation (business registration, tax certificates, licenses) over utility bills when compiling reinstatement appeal evidence.
For service-area profiles, include vehicle signage, business cards, or company apparel as photographic supporting evidence in reinstatement appeals.
If an initial reinstatement appeal is rejected, resubmit with additional documentation or file multiple help tickets to increase approval likelihood.
Use video verification rather than address-based or service-area configuration when creating new profiles to reduce future suspension risk.
Write down every task assignment with a timestamp (email is ideal) immediately after giving the verbal instruction; never rely on a verbal-only request for anything that must be done.
When assigning work with a deadline, ask the assignee: how long will the actual work take (not how long until you can deliver it), and what else do you have on your schedule between now and then.

Use end-of-day as your personal default delivery expectation and explicitly set it as the default for your team; only accept end-of-week or later when the assignee can demonstrate a specific competing obligation that is genuinely more important.

Apply the Document-Demonstrate-Duplicate method for any skill transfer: write the steps as a checklist while performing the task yourself, then do those steps in front of the trainee, then have the trainee do those same steps in front of you before declaring skill transferred.

When a team member is underperforming, run through the five STAR questions in order before concluding motivation is the issue; most non-performance is resolved at steps 1-4 (awareness, definition, training, deadline) rather than step 5 (circumstances) or motivation.

Replace declarative impossibility statements (no one can do X like me) with how questions (how would I find someone who can do X like me) to open solvable search processes instead of closed cognitive loops.

To find your free lead magnet: (1) identify what competitors charge for, (2) calculate your hard cost to deliver it, (3) give it away for free, (4) measure lead volume, (5) measure conversion. Make it better than what others charge for.
When building a marketing department, maintain a tight team of the highest-leverage people with performance incentives, rather than adding headcount to cover ground. Fewer, better.
Every founder must personally know how to get customers and how to deliver to customers at a basic level; everything else can be outsourced.

To identify your growth allocation priority, ask: What would it take for us to be number one in our market? Then ask: Do we have the resources to make that happen? Then ask: Why are we not putting every resource toward that right now?

For advertising and educational video, spend the majority of production time in pre-production (concept, hook, examples, sequence) and minimize post-production editing. Notes and structure before recording; avoid winging it and cutting in post.

Rank split tests in this priority order: (1) offer, (2) packaging and headlines, (3) images, (4) third-party tool integrations. Test third-party integrations despite the operational complexity; they yield the largest unlocks.

Before designing an affiliate program, strip out a single component of your core offer and give the affiliate 100% of revenue from that component, rather than giving them a percentage cut of your main offer. Set a minimum price floor to maintain customer quality.

Surface any genuine negative about your business or offer proactively in marketing (small team, limited parking, not the most experienced) and use the damaging admission format: [negative], but [relevant positive that amplifies]. Frame the negative as a feature for the right audience.

To increase LTV: raise prices (the single strongest lever), add retention mechanisms, and build upsell paths. Do not accept the industry-average CAC as a constraint; diagnose whether the real problem is LTV.
Promote just enough to get initial consumption (people trying the product), then pause promotion and improve the product iteratively based on customer feedback before scaling marketing spend further.

Survey customers constantly to identify what can improve; analyze onboarding friction and time-to-value; measure whether results happen faster and easier each iteration; add so much value that customers cannot compare you to any competitor.

When customers begin referring business, add mechanisms to make it harder to leave: in B2B, add collateral or control the money flow (integrate payment processing, require prepayment, or structure it so you process funds upfront).

Treat every payment failure or service complaint as a feedback loop to eliminate the underlying problem, not as evidence that customers are lazy or irresponsible; take full responsibility for product quality.

Structure business models to collect payment before or immediately upon purchase (prepayment or payment-on-delivery), and use royalties or revenue-share structures that take payment off the top before remitting to operators.

Establish customer surplus—deliver value so far exceeding the price that customers fear losing the deal and call ahead of time to ensure continuous service; this psychological state is the goal of retention strategy.

Before pitching, ask the prospect: why are they there, what is the problem, what have they tried and failed, and why they think those attempts failed. Use this to position your product as different from the things that failed.

Expose your sales team weekly to recent customer testimonials — in person or via video — describing how their lives have changed since buying. Schedule this before or during active sales appointment blocks.
topic: Daily Sales Role-Play as Training Cadence

text: When a prospect raises an objection, pause, slow your breathing, and respond with a curious question ('Huh, that's interesting — tell me more about that') rather than a counter-argument or solution pitch.
Use a no-based close phrasing: 'Would you mind moving forward today?' rather than 'Do you want to sign up?' — the opt-out framing reduces resistance for confrontation-averse prospects.
Explain your product exclusively through the experiences the prospect will have as a result, not through features. Use analogies to make unfamiliar future experiences concrete.

When building a sales team, set a very short tolerance window for underperformance (approximately one week) and turn over reps who do not show early promise quickly — this keeps the team composition at elite level and the team itself aware of performance standards.
Ask family members, friends, or acquaintances if you can use their aged Gmail account to create a Google Business Profile; prioritize accounts with 5+ years of activity.
Use different devices for each verification attempt (e.g., phone for one attempt, computer for another); avoid using the same device on the same Wi-Fi network for multiple rapid attempts.

Do not purchase aged Gmail accounts from third-party sellers; use trusted personal accounts only because purchased accounts are often recycled or created in bulk outside the US (increasing spam-filter risk).
Target service categories with low regulatory liability (cleaning, landscaping, detailing) before attempting categories requiring licensing or bonding (plumbing, electrical).

To scale lead generation, pay young people ($10 per attempt is mentioned as viable) to use their phones for verification attempts; college campuses and social networks are cited as recruiting sources.

Immediately after launching a GMB profile, complete all optimization tasks within the first week: gather reviews, add photos, write a complete description, optimize title with location keywords, ensure good website SEO, purchase citations and backlinks, and respond to all reviews.
Do not make multiple edits to a GMB profile in a single day; spread optimization work over time to avoid triggering Google's suspension mechanisms.

For a service niche, research the local top 3-5 ranked competitors on Google Maps, identify their review counts and ratings, and target matching or exceeding their review count while optimizing SEO title and description to outrank them.

When filming a before/after short-form clip, add a 30-second verbal overlay with a pain-based hook (e.g., 'if you struggle with X, this is something we do all the time at our clinic') without revealing the patient's name; cover eyes if needed for privacy.
Take a photo of every patient at intake, at day 30, and at day 60; treat each patient as a potential before/after post rather than waiting for exceptional cases.
Run organic content on Instagram and TikTok first; identify the highest-performing piece by engagement; attach a CTA to that piece and run it as a paid ad with an offer.

Before associating your brand with any advertiser, endorser, or partner, apply a personal acid-test: would you send your sister, your mom, or a close friend there? If the answer is no, decline the relationship regardless of revenue.
Never risk the empire for a pot of gold — no single advertiser relationship or revenue opportunity should be pursued if it can damage the foundational trust asset of the business.
Play incremental long ball — look for the accumulated value of many small experiments and iterations rather than waiting for a singular home run or breakthrough deal.
When doubt exists on capital deployment, take the profits home and invest in mutual funds or real estate rather than deploying internally into a low-conviction internal project.
Pour resources into content formats and platforms that show measurable results; do not invest in platforms because they are new or popular — allocate based on demonstrated audience response.

For educators and coaches: identify the actual customer need from early cohort data (who shows up, what problem they actually have) rather than the problem you designed the product to address, and rebuild the curriculum around observed need.

To implement the loss leader strategy: itemize every component of your offer (e.g., facility access, accountability, workouts, nutrition guides), select one component to promote at 80-90% off, market that single component aggressively, then upsell the full bundle once the prospect engages.

When executing the gift card referral strategy, collect the contact information of the recipient at the point of gift card sale, then use it to send a three-way introduction between the existing customer and the new prospect, enabling follow-up if the gift card is never redeemed.

For high-ticket scarcity drops, build advance hype before the launch date, announce the exact time the offer goes live, instruct prospects to have credit cards ready, then publicly announce remaining unit counts after each sale to sustain FOMO momentum.

When launching a new facility or service and using the prepay buy X get Y free promotion, limit the promotion to the first 50 or 100 buyers to de-risk fulfillment and capture immediate cash to cover opening costs without drawing on reserves.

Apply the MAGIC wrapper to every holiday promotion by naming the avatar explicitly, stating the dream outcome and the time interval, and using a container word (blueprint, accelerator, program, intensive, launchpad, getaway) to bucket all offer components into a single branded product name.

For recurring membership businesses using prepay promotions, require full upfront payment at the discounted price and do not offer a payment plan; the entire business rationale of the prepay discount is cash collected immediately.

When you get home, order your to-do list from the item requiring the least input to produce the highest output, and begin executing them in that order — ignoring new ideas that sound exciting until the existing list is done.
topic: The Execution Gap: Knowledge Without Action

text: Split test landing pages, emails, and ads not once but weekly — install a repeatable process for continuous improvement rather than single-event optimization.
Role-play sales and customer success scenarios not once but daily, so every representative builds hundreds of practice reps on objections, refunds, and pricing conversations.
Take ten more candidate interviews for the same role than you planned — the expected additional time lost in evaluation is far less than the six months lost by hiring the wrong person and restarting.
Ask yourself regularly: 'If I were coaching me, what would I tell me to do?' Act on that answer rather than what feels more stimulating.
topic: The Execution Gap: Knowledge Without Action

text: Commit to daily prospecting activity independent of whether recent results were up or down — divorce the activity identity from the outcome, because who you are is forged in the repetitive act.

Ask every employee three questions in order: (1) What do you do? (push for specific activities, not amorphous descriptors like 'analyze'), (2) Do you know what we do as a business? (verify they can explain the business model), (3) How does what you do help what we do? (tie their inputs to business outputs). Employees who cannot answer the third question are likely not contributing to revenue generation.

When overwhelmed, list every activity on your plate for the week, then ask: does this tie directly to increasing the number of customers or increasing lifetime value per customer? Remove or defer everything that does neither.

When you find a working referral or affiliate system, immediately invest in reducing activation friction further: streamline the referral process, improve training, remove steps, and make it easier for people who are already motivated to refer to actually do so.

Build brand by making promises and consistently over-delivering on them. Do not rely on visual branding (logos, colors, fonts) as a substitute; brand is the aggregate of how many people trust you based on accumulated positive experiences.

Measure the cost of every meeting by multiplying the number of attendees by their effective hourly rate (annual salary divided by 2,000). A 10-person meeting is a $500 spend. Require that every meeting produce a return of at least 4-5x its cost, or do not hold it.

Set your Facebook Marketplace account location to the same city where your business profile is located (or where you want the profile ranked) before posting the $25 gift card offer. This ensures that recruited reviewers are from the correct geographic region and that their reviews will pass Google's locality validation.
Post a $25 gift card (or direct cash transfer) offer on Facebook Marketplace with the exact phrase 'not a scam' in the title or description to increase response rate from interested participants.

Start by offering reviewers $5 per review and propose they do one review first as a test to verify you're not scamming them. This reduces friction and increases the likelihood they'll do additional reviews or recruit their friends and family.

When recruiting reviewers, follow up with a pre-written template message explaining the incentive structure, allowing you to efficiently scale outbound communication without having to craft custom responses.

Budget approximately $5 per review for the incentive; the total investment to generate 100 reviews would be around $500. This investment is justifiable when the business model can generate $10,000+ monthly profit from the resulting ranked profile.

Use the ACA framework in sales and social conversations: Acknowledge what the other person just said, Compliment what their statement reveals about a positive attribute they possess, then Ask the next question to keep them engaged and moving through the conversation.

In brick-and-mortar businesses, screenshot every five-star review from Yelp and other platforms, frame them, and cover the lobby walls floor-to-ceiling with those reviews alongside before/after photos to create a physical social-proof environment that preemptively neutralizes skepticism.

Display diplomas, certifications, and awards prominently in your business; in industries where certifications are unaccredited (e.g., US fitness), obtain and display multiple certifications — including internally issued ones — to raise perceived authority through volume.

Get the small yes before asking for the big yes: use lead magnets, low-commitment front-end offers, or simple public questions (e.g., asking someone if they are the type who takes action) to establish a voluntary identity commitment before making the primary close.

When facing real capacity limits, state them explicitly to prospects: telling customers the actual number of spots, units, or time remaining available sells more than leaving limits implicit, because authentic scarcity is more believable and activates loss aversion more reliably.

Frame promotional offers using loss language rather than gain language: say 'you don't want to miss out on' rather than 'don't you want to get' to exploit loss aversion and increase purchase motivation.

Before any negotiation, obtain at least one credible alternative offer or position so you genuinely do not need the deal on the table. For employment negotiations, get a competing job offer before negotiating with your current employer. For vendor negotiations, collect multiple bids before committing. For M&A, have multiple interested buyers before selling.

When presenting a BATNA overtly to a counterpart, give them a clear choice: beat the competing offer or don't waste each other's time. Alternatively, keep the alternative private and use it only as internal psychological grounding to anchor higher and hold longer.
Always anchor first if possible; set the initial number as high as defensible so the negotiation range shifts in your favor before the counterpart has made their first offer.

After accepting a deal where the counterpart anchored first, tell them you wouldn't have done it for any less (or more) — this eliminates buyer's remorse and protects the relationship even if the first anchor left money on the table.
When a contractor or vendor makes a mistake, ask them what it would cost them to fix it rather than asking for a discount. Their answer becomes the self-anchored concession value.

When a counterpart presents multiple simultaneous offers, ask for an Option D that combines the best element from each option, converting the seller's flexibility signal into a buyer-designed package.

Before sitting down to negotiate, enumerate every variable in the deal beyond price (financing type, closing period, included assets, risk allocation, speed, ease, support level) and plan which variables to deploy in which order, keeping most in reserve for later rounds.

To frame a purchase as an investment rather than a cost, gather comparable data (e.g., comparable home sales, maintenance cost savings, revenue projections) before the negotiation so the ROI claim is evidence-backed rather than asserted.
Track monthly joins versus cancels, label the business growing, flat, or declining based on whether joins exceed, match, or fall below cancels.

Message every canceling customer to ask why they canceled. Tag each reason (price, overwhelm, not using, missing feature, not what I expected) in a spreadsheet. For every ~20 cancels, review the top one or two reasons and fix those.
Identify the longest-tenured, most-engaged members and ask them what one thing made them stay. Whatever shows up repeatedly becomes the retention engine; everything else is optional.

Survey your customers: ask what one thing they would fight to keep if everything else were deleted, and what one thing they would not mind losing. Chart the results to identify the two highest-value elements; focus exclusively on those.
Create an explicit start-here or weekly-cadence flow for busy members while leaving optional deep-dive side quests for power users.
Front-load the stickiest element of your product in onboarding so new members encounter it as quickly as possible, ideally within the first 24 hours.
Show up in your community or customer-facing channel daily: clear notifications, respond to DMs, review complaints, reinforce good behavior publicly, and remove disruptive members.
Default to one high-value weekly communication touchpoint (e.g., a live call plus a best-of post) rather than multiple lower-engagement ones.
Add an annual plan at a 16-17% discount (buy 10 months, get 2 free) and announce it to your existing member base to stabilize retention immediately.
topic: Setup Fee as Churn Reduction Mechanism

text: Identify the top 10 most engaged members (model citizens), DM them to understand their goals, spotlight them publicly, invite them to contribute, and introduce new members to them by name with a brief context on shared interests.
Do not overhaul your entire business because month-one churn is high; high early-tenure churn is normal and does not require a complete product change unless virtually all new members are leaving.
When starting with no proof in a high-ticket service business, offer free work to build your first testimonials before attempting paid sales.
Give prospects your personal cell phone number and emphasize that you are the owner-operator doing the work directly, to compensate for absence of track record.
Explicitly tell prospects that you need testimonials and case studies so they understand your incentive is fully aligned with their success.
Structure free client engagements as a fixed number of sessions (e.g., five calls) with a defined conversion decision point at the end, not open-ended free service.
Increase prospecting volume when facing repeated prospect hesitation with no proof; volume compensates for low individual conversion probability at this stage.

E-commerce founders should forecast cash flow using inventory cycle lead times, predicting sales volume 12 weeks out to ensure sufficient inventory capital. Without this forecasting discipline, a business with strong demand can still stall because it runs out of inventory while waiting for reorders.

E-commerce businesses should build redundancy into every supply chain node: multiple raw material suppliers, multiple manufacturers, and multiple 3PL providers across geographies so that a single vendor failure does not halt the entire operation.

Service business owners should invest heavily in structured recruitment, onboarding, and training systems before scaling marketing or sales, because talent supply is the binding constraint and cannot be solved with more leads.
Service business owners should define clear career paths for their talent to reduce attrition; people who are hard to recruit and expensive to train are even more expensive to lose.

Education business owners should explicitly price the consumable recurring elements of their offering (community, updated content, continued-education resources) separately and at a price proportionate to the value those elements deliver monthly, not at a price designed to pay off the one-time knowledge product over time.
SaaS founders should obsess over product quality and customer feedback before scaling marketing or sales, because poor activation and churn will neutralize any acquisition investment.

SaaS founders should build viral or referral loops into the product from early on so that each acquired user generates more than one additional user, compounding down the blended cost of acquisition as scale increases.

Any business owner should frame the core structural difficulty of their model (cash flow in e-commerce, talent in service, stickiness in education, product-market fit in SaaS) as the value-creating problem that, if solved, generates the most enterprise value, rather than as evidence that something is wrong.

Dedicate the first four hours of every working day exclusively to one chosen outreach or advertising method (warm outreach, cold outreach, paid ads, or content) until revenue exceeds $1 million; do not split focus across multiple methods.

Run any marketing copy, ad script, email, or landing page text through a reading grade-level tool and revise until it scores below fifth grade (third grade is the target); send only after reaching that benchmark.
Before entering any new market or launching any new product, invest time working for free in exchange for testimonials, reviews, and feedback to build a proof base before charging at scale.
When responding to online hate or competitor attacks publicly, begin with agreement ('you are right') and optionally add a compliment; do not enumerate counter-arguments or defend specific points.

When scaling any proven advertising or outreach channel, first confirm that the existing creative and copy are held constant; then multiply volume (budget, contacts, posting frequency) 2x, 5x, or 10x before introducing any variation.

Identify a single attribute of your business that no competitor has publicly claimed, narrow it until it is uniquely yours in positioning, and lead all advertising with that specific claim rather than generic superiority statements.

Review your top-performing content and ads to identify the highest-converting hook; allocate 70% of future production to carbon copies of that hook, 20% to adjacent variations, and only 10% to entirely new experiments.

Diagnose rising cost-per-lead by checking whether cost-per-thousand-impressions (CPM) is also rising; if CPM is flat but CPL is up, investigate whether negative word of mouth is pre-disqualifying would-be buyers before they respond.

Ensure that at least 70% of all advertising impressions delivered are brand/education/give-value content rather than direct offers or calls-to-action; reserve no more than 30% of impression budget for direct sales asks.

To diagnose whether a business is supply- or demand-constrained, answer four yes/no questions: (1) If more customers showed up tomorrow, could you serve them at your standard? (2) Are you turning away business or maintaining waiting lists? (3) Are your most profitable time slots or products always sold out? (4) Do you run out of inventory or have long shipping delays? Any yes answer indicates a supply problem.

For supply-constrained service businesses: (1) raise prices first (fastest fix), (2) add capacity through technology (one person doing 5x the work), (3) train existing staff from level B to level A performance, or (4) hire additional staff at the same skill level to run parallel capacity.

For demand-constrained businesses: fix the acquisition channel first (outreach, ads, affiliates, content), then fix conversion rate at each funnel stage (lead capture, show rate, close rate), then fix offer and pricing if the demand leak is at those stages.

When organic content has generated confirmed sales, take the best-performing organic content, add a five-second CTA at the end, and run it as a paid ad rather than producing bespoke creative for paid channels.

For physical product businesses in a supply constraint episode, reach out to existing customers and sell intangible products (warranties, software subscriptions, affiliate-sourced digital products) to generate cash that can be used to pay vendors a premium (approximately 20%) to jump the fulfillment queue.

Train home services technicians with a two- to three-line upsell script and conduct daily role-play to track upsell percentage; measure what percentage of completed jobs convert to a second service and iterate the script until the rate reaches 50% or above.

In complex B2B sales where the economic decision-maker and the operational decision-maker are different people, re-script the sales process to focus on elevating the status and self-interest of the operational decision-maker, not just securing approval from the economic buyer.

When doing CEO cold outreach to recruit executive candidates, use an intro message framed as a referral ask: 'You seem perfect. Do you know anyone exactly like you? I have this great role that pays X.' This framing is lower-pressure than a direct pitch and frequently results in self-nomination.

When multiple leadership roles are unfilled, rank them by operational damage (which missing role is causing the most fires today) and fill them in that order rather than all at once, to keep onboarding quality high and the founder's management bandwidth stable.

Reframe recruiting agency fees (typically 20-25% of annual package) as capital investments with an expected return multiple, not as operational expenses, to overcome cost-avoidance instincts that prevent necessary senior hiring.

For technical or unfamiliar leadership roles, engage existing trusted domain experts (attorneys, accountants, technical leads already on retainer) to conduct competency interviews on your behalf; reserve your own interview time for cultural fit and organizational judgment.

When selecting a city for a new service-area Google Business Profile, run a search-volume analysis for all intent-aligned keyword variations (e.g., 'plumber,' 'plumbing,' 'plumbing company,' 'plumbing services' + city name); exclude supply-chain or non-customer-intent keywords ('plumbing supply store').

Before committing to a city, manually audit the current three-pack businesses to count reviews, identify ranking incumbents, and assess whether entry is feasible (1-2 businesses with <100 reviews indicates exploitable gap).

Conduct a secondary check on contractor availability: search for existing service providers in the target city to confirm that 3+ contractors are available and not fully booked. Very small towns may have sufficient search volume but insufficient supply-side capacity.

Verify that the target neighborhood has a healthy demographic profile with reasonable payment propensity; avoid areas with high payment-default risk even if search volume is high, as default risk compresses unit economics.

Sell based on the value you create for the buyer, not the cost it costs you to deliver. Ask: what is this worth to them? Then eliminate risk, shorten time delay, and reduce required effort to close the gap between that value and what they will pay.

Structure your pricing and upsell sequence so that 30-day cash collected equals at least 2x (CAC + COGS). If your current model does not achieve this, redesign the offer sequence — add a front-end upsell, introduce quarterly prepayment with a baked-in discount, or add an onboarding fee — before scaling acquisition spend.

Never allow industry payment norms (e.g., net-60) to dictate your cash conversion cycle. Offer buyers a prepayment incentive (e.g., 5% discount for quarterly billing, added onboarding service) to pull cash forward. The discount is baked into the price; the cash timing improvement funds growth.

When a prospect declines your primary offer, immediately identify the underlying problem they are trying to solve (not the specific solution they rejected) and make a different offer that addresses the same problem in a format they prefer. Do not walk away from a no without testing an adjacent offer.

Segment your customer base into permanent (2+ year) and transient customers. Identify the demographic and behavioral profile of permanent customers, then build advertising specifically targeting that avatar even if it doubles the CAC — the improvement in permanent conversion rate will reduce effective permanent CAC.

Track enterprise value multiple alongside cash income. For recurring-revenue businesses, do not optimize for after-tax cash at the expense of customer retention and ARR growth — the enterprise value multiple on retained ARR creates far more untaxed wealth than any income tax strategy.
Document your struggle in real time, even when you are ashamed of where you are. Treat the current difficult chapter as footage you will want later when telling your story.
When someone calls your effort cringe, interpret that as a signal you are shifting relative status — and therefore evidence you are on the right path, not the wrong one.
topic: Shame vs. Guilt: Navigating Social Signals

text: Do not judge your first chapter by someone else's 25th or 1,000th chapter. Compare only within the same stage of a journey.

Write down the name of any team member whose performance you know is inadequate and initiate a 14-day Performance Improvement Plan: state the specific behaviors that must change within 14 days or the person exits.
When managing a team, say directly to the person's face what you currently say about them behind their back. Do not soften, qualify, or defer the conversation.
When evaluating any proposed initiative, ask: does this get us more customers, make customers worth more, or reduce the risk that the first two stop happening? If it maps to none of these, cut it.

Before opening new acquisition channels, ask whether the existing best channel can be doubled in volume first (More), then whether conversion, speed, or personalization can be improved without new resources (Better). Only after both are exhausted should a new channel be added (New).
Apply the Rule of 100 daily for lead generation: $100 in ad spend, OR 100 cold outreaches, OR 100 warm outreaches, OR 100 minutes of content — pick one and do it every day without exception.
When evaluating a business constraint, ask: why can't we 10x this business? The answer usually immediately reveals the actual binding constraint.

Before investing in marketing, verify that churn is low enough to justify acquisition spend: if the business would not survive three to four months without selling any new customers, fix the back end first.

When building toward multi-location or franchise scale, strip the model to its simplest operational form — minimum square footage, minimum SKUs or services, minimum headcount — before replicating. Simplicity is what makes the unit economics scalable.

When upset, pause and examine the circumstance: pull it apart, ask 'is this real? Is this true? Is anyone doing this perfectly?' to reveal that most stressors are optional interpretations rather than facts.
Use the volume lever: when a negative circumstance bothers you, ask 'would I be upset if this happened every day?' or 'what if the opposite occurred?' to recalibrate meaning.
Use the time lever: ask yourself 'will this matter in 10,000 years?' and 'should it matter now?'—zooming out reduces anxiety by revealing relative insignificance.
Artificially move your internal 'middle line': ask 'what if this were worse?' and 'what if this were worse all the time?' to shift your perception of today's circumstance as relatively good.

When experiencing loss or grief, reframe using comparison: measure the actual outcome against the counterfactual baseline (what would have been without the positive deviation) to shift emotions from loss to gratitude.

When learning a new skill, define measurable success criteria before beginning practice: identify the specific observable behaviors and quantifiable outputs that constitute mastery of each sub-skill (e.g., for foul shots: percentage of shots within the box, percentage made, shoulder alignment, follow-through height).
Deconstruct any skill you want to learn down to its atomic observable behavioral units before beginning practice; do not attempt to learn 'business' or 'basketball' as a whole.

When evaluating teachers or coaches, use this razor: if they cannot tell you what to do with your mouth or your body, they are not providing actionable instruction and should be deprioritized as learning sources.
Look at what top performers do, not what they say about what they do; observe behavior, not self-reported explanations.

Remove luck from your explanatory vocabulary when analyzing why someone outperforms you; treat their advantage as the result of behaviors you have not yet performed and search for what those behaviors are.
topic: Effort Compounds Relative to Starting Conditions

text: Prioritize building generalizable skills (reading, writing, speaking, learning itself) as these multiply the rate of acquisition across all future domain-specific skills.
When entering a new domain cold, hire a domain expert as a starting-point accelerator to begin at an advanced iteration rather than from scratch; then exceed them by applying a faster feedback loop.

Use the Start-Stop-Keep feedback format when diagnosing culture or giving team feedback: specify what you want someone to start doing that they are not doing, stop doing that they are currently doing, and keep doing that is already working. This operationalizes culture critique into actionable behavioral directives.

When diagnosing why a business plan is not being executed, identify whether the root cause is culture (reinforcement rules are wrong), talent (people quality is insufficient), or training (abstract goals have not been converted to observable behaviors) before changing strategy.

During hiring interviews, ask candidates what they do in their off time and what they are obsessed with. Use this to determine whether their discretionary effort flows toward the skill required by the role.

When evaluating abstract leadership or culture terms like 'accountability,' press yourself to describe the observable behaviors that would constitute that term in action — what would a third party see happening? Replace the abstract term in training and feedback with those observable behaviors.

Before switching business strategy, diagnose whether the constraint is cultural, talent-based, or training-based; solve the present constraint on the current path before abandoning it, because switching paths resets accumulated progress to zero.
When raising capital from accredited investors without a personal network, start with conferences and events before other channels unless you already have a background in media buying.
topic: Conferences and Events as High-Leverage Channels

text: Treat an investor acquisition funnel as an enterprise sale: apply the same trust-building, qualification, and closing mechanics regardless of whether the product is a service or an investment vehicle.
When evaluating capital-raising channels, classify trade shows under the affiliate model (paying for access to someone else's audience) rather than as a standalone channel.

To recruit a first salesperson for a roofing company, offer a stated commission rate, demonstrate the door-knocking acquisition method, and allow the recruit to earn on results. No complex compensation structure or formal HR process is required at early stage.
When transitioning from solo sales to team sales, stop measuring yourself by your personal close rate and start measuring yourself by your team's close rate.
When you receive a bad Google review, immediately click off the current activity and address it following the removal framework without delay.
To verify your local guide level, log into the Google Maps app, click your profile picture, select 'profile,' and check the local guide level displayed.

To recruit other account holders to report a review on your behalf, click 'share review,' copy the review link, and send it to people you know are active on Google, asking them to report it using the bullying and harassment category.

Before evaluating any adjacent business model, ask: if the downside scenario happens and the new model fails while the existing business degrades, can you live with that outcome? If not, do not proceed.

In insurance-reimbursed service businesses, audit COGS and operational costs before exploring expansion; a 10-point margin improvement on existing locations delivers greater dollar profit than opening multiple new locations at current margins.
Do not pursue a licensing model until new locations open at a rate of at least one per quarter using a dedicated opening team that does not include the founder.

When evaluating M&A vs. greenfield for location growth, preference acquisitions of existing practices: the existing staff, clientele, and infrastructure compress conversion timeline to your operating metrics by roughly half.

When competitors who are well-funded with talented teams have failed to make a new model profitable, treat this as strong evidence of structural model difficulty rather than an execution gap you can close.
If a defined short-program ad campaign was previously working, return to it rather than replacing it with a direct ongoing-service offer when conversion drops.

When building a tutoring offer, state the specific measurable outcome (e.g., a 4-point score improvement or top-10% state ranking) and attach a free-continuation guarantee until the outcome is achieved.
Bundle a short defined front-end program against a full-year package (not a single term) to set the expectation of the full engagement from the first sale.

When Facebook platform targeting restrictions prevent isolating the economically responsible buyer (e.g., parents vs. students), prioritize fixing the audience definition before optimizing creative or offer.

Read the affiliates chapter in $100M Leads ($29) before building or restructuring a white-label or affiliate distribution layer; the chapter outlines a two-pronged launch-plus-retention distributor strategy.

Before concluding that a business needs more leads or marketing spend, diagnose whether existing customers are churning and calculate what retention improvement would deliver if compounded over three years.

When distributor agencies are churning from a white-label service, first determine whether churn is due to non-usage or poor quality before changing pricing or marketing; non-usage churn requires a usage activation intervention, not a quality fix.

When you want to change an abstract personal trait (be more authentic, more patient, more courageous), first translate the trait into a specific observable behavior you must start or stop. Ask: what would someone do for me to say this trait has occurred?
When diagnosing a persistent unwanted behavior in yourself or others, examine what was rewarded immediately after the behavior the last time it occurred, not what triggered it beforehand.

When giving feedback on a person's character or attitude (e.g., they are lazy, aggressive, disrespectful), trace the complaint back to two to three specific observable acts and communicate only those acts, not the abstract label.
To build a new replacement behavior, create a reinforcement signal as quickly as possible after the new behavior occurs. Reward proximity accelerates the replacement of the old reinforcement loop.

Apply B.F. Skinner's principle that if many variables exist, many variables must be studied: resist the urge to collapse multi-dimensional traits into binary labels (honest or dishonest, authentic or inauthentic) and instead measure them on a continuum.
Start producing content immediately (ASAP) in any service niche, regardless of brand size, to build the pool of creative assets from which ad winners can be identified.
When running a webinar funnel, end the presentation with an explicit solicitation for attendees to book a one-on-one call; do not rely on passive opt-ins.
Route traffic from winning content directly to the offer (call or webinar), not to a generic homepage or brand page.
Record every sales call. Review hot-streak recordings when performance dips to re-enter optimal tonality and pacing without guesswork.
topic: Daily Sales Role-Play as Training Cadence

text: At the end of every sales call, ask for a referral using the phrasing 'Who do you know who is as awesome as you?' to embed a compliment into the referral request and force a name-shaped answer rather than a yes/no.
Maintain a kill list of high-value whale prospects separate from your CRM, placed somewhere visible daily, so high-priority follow-up never falls behind lower-volume routine outreach.
Do 5-10% of call duration in research before every sales call. For a 60-minute call, invest 6 minutes of preparation on the prospect's business, role, and recent activity.
Read fresh customer testimonials aloud to the sales team at the daily opening meeting to replenish conviction after a day of rejection.
topic: Daily Sales Role-Play as Training Cadence

text: Never allow a call to end without the next meeting booked (BAMFAM: Book A Meeting From A Meeting). Address any scheduling hesitation as an obstacle to resolve on the current call.
Separate setters and closers for inbound and outbound lead streams as soon as volume permits; using one team for both degrades conversion on both lead types.
Send a personalized video or voice memo from the sales rep the day before an appointment, referencing specific context from the prospect's situation, to maximize show rates for booked calls.
topic: Show-Up Rate and Lead Nurture Optimization

text: When a prospect cannot make a decision, walk them through three confronting questions: (1) Do you believe this product will help you achieve your goal? (2) Do you trust me to deliver what I said? (3) Do you believe it will work specifically for you? Only ask for the sale after receiving three affirmatives.
Give the best leads to the best closers by scoring lead quality and matching it to rep close-rate tiers; do not distribute leads randomly across the team.

When pitching franchise opportunities, present actual financial data from existing open locations (as disclosed in the FDD) rather than making forward-looking promises. Let the unit economics speak for themselves.

Before investing in franchise sales and marketing, spend dedicated time (Hormozi suggests ~24 months) optimizing per-location profitability down to the penny. Only pursue franchise growth once unit economics are genuinely compelling.

When evaluating a franchise versus corporate expansion strategy, model both paths fully to exit proceeds — including royalty rate, franchisor EBITDA margins, exit multiple, and rollover requirement — before committing to the franchise path.

Print two copies of the sales script. On one copy, read aloud and enunciate every word fully. After completing the full read, black out one word and read again. Repeat, blacking out one additional word each pass, until the entire page is blacked out and you are reciting the script from memory.
After making the close ask (the invitation to buy), stop talking and do not fill the silence for up to eight seconds. Wait for the prospect to respond.

When a prospect gives one-word or vague answers in discovery, alternate between two probes: 'Can you give me an example of that?' and 'Can you be more specific?' Repeat until you have a concrete problem statement with enough detail to chunk up to a solvable category.

Once you have two to three chunked-up problem categories from discovery, recap them explicitly to the prospect and get verbal confirmation before transitioning: 'So it sounds like you have a marketing problem and a pricing problem. Is that fair to say?' Then ask if solving those would grow their business. Only proceed to the pitch after a yes.

Use only three punctuation marks to annotate vocal behavior in a sales script: period (full stop), ellipsis (short pause, draw attention), and question mark (rising intonation, solicit a response). Do not add prose tone-direction notes; they are unactionable.
topic: Process Design Enables Junior Talent Execution

text: When coaching a salesperson who sounds nervous or speaks too fast, do not say 'sound more confident.' Say 'speak at a slower cadence' or 'fully pronounce each word.' Observable behavior instructions replace abstract emotional directives.

When you are poor and starting out, scan every line item in your expenses and proactively barter your service or inventory for anything you need — cleaning, printing, food, laundry — to preserve cash for revenue-generating activities.

Do not pretend to have resources or results you do not have when starting a business; admitting you need help makes people far more likely to assist you, especially other entrepreneurs who are one to two steps ahead.

When asking clients whether they followed a plan or protocol, do not accept binary yes/no answers; ask specific quantitative follow-up questions (e.g., how many days out of seven did you complete all three meals exactly to plan?) to surface actual adherence rates rather than perception-filtered answers.

In sales conversations, focus on the pain of the prospect's current situation and the vivid positive experience of the desired outcome; do not describe the steps required to get there (the process), as this creates objections rather than motivation.

When hiring an agency for a capability you lack, explicitly declare your intention to learn the skill so you can eventually replace them; negotiate an hourly teaching arrangement if the agency will not sell you learning access in their standard engagement.

Screenshot all five-star reviews from Google and Yelp, print them in dollar-store frames, and display them in your sales area to surround prospects with overwhelming social proof during the conversation.

Pair authority with responsibility equally when delegating to operators: explicitly grant a spending threshold (e.g., up to $1,000 or up to 100% of one month's customer spend) so the operator can resolve issues without calling you.

Run an internal promotional offer to your existing customer list approximately four times per year; pick one specific component of your service to feature as a standalone add-on program to generate near-100% margin incremental revenue.

When considering a product or service upsell, first ask whether it can be structured at zero additional time or labor cost; prioritize upsells that recover advertising cost so that service revenue operates above the customer acquisition cost.

Before asking whether your business can run without you, take a one-month vacation; what breaks reveals the true dependencies and provides a concrete checklist for the systems and people needed before scaling.

Before setting a revenue growth target for the year, a service business owner should explicitly quantify what tripling net margin percentage (without growing revenue) would produce in absolute dollars, and compare that to the absolute dollars produced by hitting the revenue target at current margins.

Service business owners should obtain real-time gross operating margin data broken down by product or service line, not just at the aggregate P&L level, before making any decisions about which service lines to invest in or scale.

When hiring external revenue leaders, ensure their compensation structure and cultural orientation are explicitly aligned to net margin, not top-line revenue, and test their stated understanding of this alignment in the interview process.

Take an existing YouTube tutorial on automating a specific business task, paste the transcript into an AI assistant, ask it to help you build the automation, and follow the directions step by step. When stuck, screenshot the error or state and ask the AI what to do next. Repeat until the automation is complete.
Dedicate a focused time block (weekends, evenings, early mornings) to automating one workflow end-to-end, from the first trigger to the final output, before moving to the next workflow.

When documenting a workflow for automation, replace any step described as intuition, gut feeling, or just knowing with an observable behavior description: what specific inputs are examined, what pattern is recognized, what decision is made. This makes the step automatable.
Do not advertise to customers which AI tools or automation platforms your business uses; communicate only outcomes (faster delivery, lower cost, better quality, lower risk).

Before deploying an AI sales agent, ensure that the underlying human sales process (motion, script, qualification criteria, objection handling) is already working; then apply equivalent training investment to the AI as you would to a new human hire.

Write down the actions that would guarantee you lose, flip each to its positive opposite, then decompose each positive trait into specific observable micro-behaviors that can be practiced and measured directly.

Measure your performance by whether you completed the committed actions — not by outcomes. Outcomes are lagging indicators outside your full control; action completion is leading and 100% controllable.

To change motivation, change who you compare yourself to — specifically, compare yourself to the future version of yourself you want to become rather than peers at your current level, to expand the perceived gap and increase drive.

When stuck on an instruction or goal, break it into progressively smaller steps until you reach a step you can execute without ambiguity. Never let ego prevent acknowledging that a step is not yet understood.

Build script confidence in the actual performance context — with a live person, on a real call — not in a mirror or analogous setting, because confidence is domain-specific and transfers only within the context where it was built.

Write down every task you perform at the most granular level possible (not role buckets like run ads but specific sub-tasks like make campaigns, set budgets, analyze results, write copy, test landing page headlines). Then take each task one at a time, put it into AI, ask how to automate it, take the first step from its answer, and if you get stuck screenshot your screen and ask the AI what to do next.

Take a full weekend and commit entirely to building something with an AI agent. Do not read articles about AI; get your hands into it directly. The goal is not to finish a complete project but to remove the psychological barrier and gain direct experience.

Before hiring for any role, write down the four to ten things that person would actually do with their hands and time, then ask whether each of those activities could live inside a workflow instead of headcount.

When training an AI agent on a writing or communication task, always provide explicit rules (what the output must never do) and multiple examples of the desired output style before asking it to produce anything.
Allocate at least 20% of your time to attempting to automate your own current role; the goal is to control the automation of your job rather than be replaced by someone else who does it first.
Design product packaging and retail context to align with target customer perception and willingness-to-pay. The same product in different formats commands dramatically different prices.
Run daily boiler room role-play sessions for sales teams, rotating through each stage of the sales script on a weekly cycle, with the fifth day reserved for whichever stage is currently weakest.
topic: Daily Sales Role-Play as Training Cadence

text: When selling to professional-credential audiences who resist the word 'sales,' ban the word internally and replace it with neutral alternatives ('consulting,' 'consults') to reduce identity conflict and improve activation.

To identify your best-fit avatar for a coaching business, analyze activated vs. churned cohorts across three dimensions: demographics, quantifiables (business size, revenue), and behaviors (what activated customers did that churned look-alikes did not), then restrict acquisition to only the high-activation avatar.

In an information or coaching business, charge the one-time skill-building component at a high price and the ongoing consumables at a much lower continuity price point; do not attempt to charge continuity rates for something that has near-zero value once mastered.
Invite your personal network to live launch events for maximum attendance and energy.

When you are uncertain whether to pursue a risky opportunity, explicitly ask both failure-case and success-case questions: what changes if it does not work, and what changes if it does. The contrast usually reveals the attempt is worth making because the failure case changes nothing while the success case changes everything.

When facing a seemingly unsolvable problem, identify whether another person has already solved it. If they have, find what you can offer them (money, favor, relational capital) to access their solution rather than treating the problem as a unique insurmountable barrier.

Add calls-to-action at the 30-second mark of YouTube videos, in the video description, in the pinned comment, and on the YouTube profile page directing viewers to the conversion platform (Instagram, landing page, or wherever leads are captured).

When a new follower arrives on a social media profile, DM them proactively with a simple binary question: are you here for free content, or do you want help with [specific problem]? Route those who say help into the sales process.

Build a VSL (video sales letter) of 5 to 7 minutes by scripting the most common questions and objections from past sales calls and presenting them as FAQs answered in plain language. Do not over-produce it; clarity matters more than production quality.

Use BANT to qualify prospects before a sales call: ask whether they can afford the fee, whether they are the decision-maker, what happens if the problem goes unsolved, and when they want to start — sell only to those who answer today or tomorrow on timing.

Create an A/B offer pairing: present the anchor option (high price, fewer terms) alongside the core offer so the core offer appears as the obviously better value. The anchor does not need to close; it exists to reframe the core offer.

When building a sales script, use the Plus-Plus-Minus-Minus structure: if you work with me, you get more good things; if you work with me, you get less bad things; if you do not work with me, you get more bad things; if you do not work with me, you get less good things.

Build the affiliate list by starting with your current avatar and asking: what other businesses serve this same customer at this same life moment? Do not limit to obvious partners; adjacent businesses (personal trainers, coaches, attorneys) may have equal or better audiences.
Rewrite funnel headlines to focus on the free offer (lead magnet) rather than the paid product; the headline should lower the commitment barrier to a first step, not close the sale.

When a prospect shows up to a sales call without having watched the VSL, maintain the call frame by pausing the call, playing the short VSL in the session ('grab a coffee, back in seven minutes'), and resuming — rather than running alternate scripts for watched vs. unwatched prospects.
Fix funnel leaks before scaling ad spend; confirming the funnel converts at an acceptable rate before increasing traffic prevents compounding waste.

When designing a price anchor tier, make it as similar as possible to the core offer but with one or two premium differentiators most buyers will not need — this maximizes cognitive anchor effect while keeping the feature gap believable.

Track and separate conversion metrics for cold traffic vs. warm/high-intent traffic; blend only when you want to assess overall business health, never to evaluate funnel performance or channel effectiveness.

When building a VSL, record a first version and get it live; then listen to sales call objections, record additional objection-answer segments, and append them to the existing VSL with a 'got some more questions, answering them now' framing.
Run pricing surveys early in a software company to explore different billing structures (usage-based, recurring, API-based) before committing to an initial pricing model.
topic: Close Rate as Pricing Calibration Signal

text: In scheduling-based businesses, give customers the most scheduling flexibility possible: open the most days, the most hours, with the finest-grained time increments — this directly drives throughput.
If building a software company as a core business, hire an in-house CTO rather than contracting a development shop.

When diagnosing a problem across a multi-unit or multi-customer business, survey the community, invite the top 20 performers on the specific metric to a call, and look for the behaviors they ALL share (intersection), not just the behaviors some of them share (union).
Roll out new products or distribution to a small test batch of existing customers first, observe results, then expand in waves to the full distribution base.
Do not scale paid advertising for a subscription product until monthly churn is below 2%; every dollar spent on acquisition while churn is high exits through the back-end.
Charge upfront before the trial period rather than attaching a card for future billing; upfront payment increases user commitment to taking the activation action.
Track trial-to-paid conversion rate and post-conversion churn as two separate metrics; never blend trial dropout into the churn figure used for business health assessment.
Set the rebate or free-month threshold at the number of activation actions that statistically predicts retention (e.g., 2-3 fence visualizations placed), not an arbitrary engagement figure.
Book a live onboarding call immediately upon trial signup and BAMFAM a follow-up to ensure the user attempts the activation action before the trial window expires.
Be transparent with new users about why the rebate or incentive exists: explain that you know once they use the product they will stay, and you are paying them to try it.

Structure business owner mentorship competitions around binary outcomes (scale or fail) with explicit 90-day windows, creating urgency and forcing prioritization of the highest-leverage scaling moves.

When diagnosing a scaling constraint, directly ask founders what they hate about their current business model; emotional signals often reveal the binding constraint (e.g., founder hatred of hourly billing reveals pricing model is the bottleneck).

Use founder's personal journey and portfolio results as the primary proof vehicle when selling access to scaling systems and guidance; retrospective success builds credibility for future scaling claims.

Train team members on AI tools across functional areas (sales, content, recruiting, operations, training) and measure output per dollar of headcount as the primary productivity metric, not activity metrics.
For email follow-up at scale, use AI composition tools (Compose AI) rather than manual drafting; copy-paste output and iterate on highest-leverage variations.
Use AI voiceover and video deepfake personalization for prospecting outreach; record one source video and let AI adapt it to thousands of prospects by name.
Deploy living-document onboarding videos via AI avatar platforms; update text, re-render video instantly, and avoid studio reshoot friction when processes change.
Use Otter AI or similar for interview note-taking; pass structured context between interview rounds so each interviewer has more signal than resume alone.
Recruit employed top talent via personalized outreach (Tavis, cold email with AI assist) rather than job-board-only sourcing, which captures only dissatisfied candidates already seeking exit.
Use calendar optimization AI (Reclaim AI) to consolidate meeting blocks and eliminate white-space gaps, recovering deep-work time for teams.

Redirect time freed by AI automation (note-taking, editing, email) toward high-leverage strategic work (narrative design, emotional framing, meeting consolidation) rather than just reducing headcount.
Place a spoken CTA at the 30% mark of every YouTube video (approximately 30 seconds) directing viewers to DM you on Instagram, rather than only at the end of the video where fewer viewers remain.

Send a DM to every new Instagram follower asking whether they are there for free content or for help; treat every person who responds that they want help as a qualified lead and route them to a sales call.
Create a VSL (5-7 minutes) that covers your process, client success outcomes, and what to expect on the consultation call; require all call prospects to watch it before their appointment.

Qualify leads using BANT (Budget, Authority, Need, Timing) rather than vanity metrics like social media follower count or streaming numbers when selling professional services to creative industry clients.
If a prospect on a high-ticket sales call is revealed to be unqualified for the core offer, immediately triage to an education product downsell rather than ending the call without a transaction.

Before accepting speaking engagements, calculate the opportunity cost as the number of sales days missed times the average revenue per sales day; require the speaking fee to cover that number plus travel costs.

Move the education product from a standalone revenue business to a community platform (e.g., Skool) that includes free onboarding calls, using those calls to triage community members toward paid services.

Ensure the cost to deliver each service engagement is below 20% of the charge to maintain 80%+ gross margin; if labor is $100/hour, delivery must be completable in under 11 hours for a $5,800 retainer.

Before switching business models, clearly define your primary goal: income (favors education/digital), or exit/asset creation (favors traditional service). Misalignment of goal and model is the root cause of most mid-journey model switches.

If switching from a traditional service business to education, sell or shut down the original business entirely before launching the education model — do not run both simultaneously, even as a test kitchen.

If you are a multi-location service business owner approaching 5 locations, invest in solving the second leadership layer (regional/area manager) rather than pivoting to an education business — the highest returns are in the next 50 locations, not a new model.

When testing a new play inside an education community, sample two members from each performance quintile (top, upper-middle, middle, lower-middle, bottom) across different geographies to get representative validity data rather than testing on top or bottom performers.

Before investing in any business, establish baseline data across show rate, offer rate, close rate, cash collected percentage, and units sold so that the largest leverage opportunities can be identified and prioritized at the constraint.

When constructing a lead nurture playbook, prioritize same-day and next-day appointment scheduling, add a morning-of reminder on the day of any appointment booked more than 24 hours in advance, and have the closer send a personalized voice memo or video text on the morning of the appointment.

In sales team role-play and training, rotate daily through each stage of the script (intro, discovery, offer, objections, looping) so each stage is drilled with enough repetition to be deliverable with correct tonality under live call conditions.
topic: Daily Sales Role-Play as Training Cadence

text: When evaluating sales director candidates, ask them what data they would plan to collect and how they would plan to fix observed problems; use the specificity of their answer as the primary screen for whether they can actually execute the role.

Add a three-way introduction call between the setter and the closer immediately after an appointment is booked, conducted via iPhone if possible, to build a relational bridge between the prospect and the closing rep before the appointment.

Pre-qualify decision-maker involvement during the discovery or nurture phase by explicitly asking whether anyone else would need to be part of the decision; if yes, reschedule the appointment to include that person rather than proceeding to a close without them.
Only create content about things you have personally done, experienced, or that are genuinely true to you — never regurgitate others' content or ideas you haven't lived.
Dedicate mornings (e.g., 4-6 a.m. to noon) exclusively to creative and deep work before taking any meetings or calls; schedule meetings in the afternoon after creative energy is spent.
Protect calendar time for unscheduled free thinking; deliberately block days without meetings to allow unexpected creative output, even if those days are volatile in productivity.
Audit your text messages for the prior week and identify contacts whose messages produce a cortisol/stress response; gradually reduce communication frequency with those people.

When evaluating what a successful peer is doing differently, ask not only what they are doing that you are not, but also what they are NOT doing that you are; the subtraction question often yields higher-value answers.
Invest only in domains where you have genuine skill and experience; outsized returns come from deploying capital in areas where you have an edge, not from diversifying into unfamiliar asset classes.
When something in your business is significantly outperforming expectations, go all-in and maximize it rather than moderating; treat it as a rare fat pitch.
Use the 85-year-old decision framework: mentally consult your future 85-year-old self for advice on major decisions to cut through fear-driven hesitation and short-term thinking.
Apply inverted thinking to any strategic problem: ask what actions would destroy the desired outcome, list them all, reverse the list, and treat the reversals as your strategic priorities.
Set quarterly growth goals at levels you can achieve and beat mid-quarter, then reset the goal higher; avoid setting goals you will consistently miss.

At 6am each morning, dedicate the first work block specifically to hiring the highest-quality salesperson available — not a junior agent fill, but a candidate whose caliber makes the founder feel they must get that person.
